name: Cook at Home
lead: Cooking at home is good for your family, your health, and your wealth
text: Cooking makes eating intentional. The ingredients you use, what, how and how much you cook, and the making and sharing together are valuable.

name: Bird Song Bathe
lead: Birds evolved to sing only when no predators are around
text: We associate birds singing with safety. Go out and soak in the bird songs. It will soothe and relax you.

name: Checkpoint
lead: When you hit a roadblock, see it as a checkpoint, not an endpoint
text: A chance to reevaluate and continue in a better direction, way, or attitude.

name: Prevention Wisdom
lead: Prevention is wisdom
text: Wise people don't solve problems. They prevent them. Invert: Decide what you don't want and make sure to avoid these things.

name: Toothache Theory
lead: Find another dentist
text: If your dentist doesn't fix your toothache, find another dentist. When stuck, keep looking... Don't stop until you solve your problem.

name: (Extra)ordinary
lead: Rather than being extra ordinary, try to do ordinary things extra ordinarily well
text: That alone is extraordinary.

name: Advice Not Orders
lead: When asked, give and take advice, not orders
text: This way your doing will be a result of your independent thinking. It's more empowering and collaborative.

name: Keep Knocking
lead: Doors of opportunity open to those who keep knocking
text: You can't just wish for doors to open. You have to show up and knock.

name: Post It Power
lead: Write ideas, thoughts, and tasks on post-it notes
text: Make sure you see them. One item per post-it. It makes things more manageable. It feels good to take down notes once completed.

name: Eye Level
lead: When speaking to anyone, get on their level
text: Look into their eyes. If they're sitting, sit. If they're standing, stand. When talking to a child, get on their level. It helps you connect.

name: Measure Reasonably
lead: Make measurable progress in reasonable time
text: Want to lose weight? Set a weight goal and give yourself time to achieve it. Measure once a day, not once an hour.

name: One Rabbit Rule
lead: Choose your rabbit
text: If you chase two rabbits, you may catch neither. Choose your rabbit and chase it. When you're done, chase the next one!

name: Sit in Circles
lead: When sitting with others, sit in a circle
text: It's the most communal way to sit. It creates a feeling of belonging, connection, and equality.

name: Use or Lose
lead: Life is never static
text: Use what you have and it will grow. Use it or lose it, whether it's talents, health, wealth, or relationships. You either shrink or grow.

name: Spot Smiles
lead: Play the smile game
text: Look around for people who are smiling, and smile back. Smiling is infectious. Catch the smile and pass it on.

name: Add Crazy
lead: Crazy things are easier to remember (Bizarreness Effect)
text: Next time you want to remember something or make it memorable, add something crazy!

name: Pygmalion Effect
lead: If you expect someone to do well, they're more likely to succeed
text: Have positive expectations.

name: Crisis Candy
lead: Hard things will happen
text: Turn your crisis into candy. Find the lesson. Ask how the experience can make you better. Don't waste a crisis. Learn from it.

name: Rear-View Mirror
lead: Want to know the future...
text: Past behaviour is a good predictor of the future. Want to know the future? Look into the past. Rear-view mirrors are clearer than windshields.

name: Succeed Small
lead: Take something that scares you and prove to yourself that you can do it
text: This gives you confidence you can do other things in that area.

name: Cheap Is Expensive
lead: Buy cheap, buy twice
text: Often, cheap things break. Spend a bit more now to save a lot later, both in money and headaches. You get what you pay for.

name: Hat Rule
lead: Someone needs to wear the hat
text: If everyone is responsible, then no one is responsible. For any project, decide who will 'wear the hat'.

name: Many Ways
lead: There are many ways to do something
text: Just because you've always done it a certain way doesn't mean it can't be done better. Keep learning, keep iterating. You may find a faster, easier, or more fun way.

name: Peel the Orange
lead: Two people fight over an orange
text: Finally, they agree to cut it in half. Later, they find out one wanted the peel for a cake, and the other wanted the fruit for juice. Dive deeper, so both can win.

name: Doubt Doubt
lead: When in doubt, doubt doubt
text: Doubt kills more dreams than failure ever will. When in doubt, do it! As long as there are no detrimental consequences...

name: What's Obvious
lead: When stuck, ask yourself: What's the obvious way?
text: Often, the most obvious answer is the best answer.

name: Hopeless Hope
lead: When facing a difficult problem, write an essay proving why it can't be solved
text: That almost always fixes it. As you're writing, you'll realise which piece is wrong in your mental puzzle.

name: Take Notes
lead: Don't trust your mind
text: We are human. We forget. When you see, hear, or are inspired by something, take notes. You'll thank yourself later.

name: Consistently Commit
lead: With commitment you start
text: With consistency you finish. Whatever the goal or project, commit and then work on it consistently.

name: Outside the Box
lead: Think outside the box
text: Question what you know to come up with new solutions. Move beyond right or wrong. Consider many different options.

name: Unsung Hero Interview
lead: Interview a friend, parent, or grandparent
text: Record a 5-10 min video. Ask about their life from 7 to 77 years. You'll learn a lot. And it's a great piece of history for generations to come.

name: One Is None
lead: One option is no option
text: You need at least two options to choose. And if you don't like either option, don't choose between losers, create a third option.

name: Your Word
lead: Choose a "Word of the year"
text: Let it guide you and give you clarity. Let it focus you on the person you want to become and what you want to achieve. A motto to live by.

name: Secret Service
lead: Do one act of service for your partner every day, but never tell them about it
text: Tiny acts of love and respect add up over time.

name: Known Unknowns
lead: It's good to know what you know
text: But it's just as important to know what you don't know. Explore what you don't know to decide what you need to brush up on.

name: Water Way
lead: If you want your life to flow, water what waters you
text: What and who gives you energy or joy? Make sure you give those people and activities time and attention.

name: Try New Things
lead: Try new things
text: You never know what you'll discover. New skills or likes you didn't know you had. You might make new friends. Worst case, you'll be one experience richer.

name: Do Learn
lead: The best way to learn, is to do
text: Want to learn tennis? Start hitting balls! When in doubt, just start. Practice learning by doing.

name: Find the Gift
lead: Everything bad has something good
text: If you choose to look. Dig to find the buried gift. Every adversity bears a hidden gift. If you choose to look. Find the good in the bad.

name: Think and Feel
lead: How you think and feel is up to you
text: No one can make you feel a certain way. They can do and say things to you. But how you think and feel is your choice.

name: All About Who
lead: Focus on the people rather than the journey or the destination
text: Nothing bad has ever come from surrounding yourself with inspiring, positive people. Find your tribe. Cherish them. The journey will reveal itself.

name: Photo Face
lead: When taking a group picture with your friends, everyone's happy and smiling
text: Whenever you walk into a room or meet someone, use your photo face. It will open doors and break the ice like a charm.

name: Generic vs Specific
lead: How to direct ambition
text: The more precisely you know where you want to go, the more focus you can direct towards it. The more vague you are, the harder it is to get there. Specific ambition gives direction. Generic ambition gives anxiety.

name: Write and Guess
lead: Before sending a message, stop
text: Take a moment to anticipate the recipient's issues or questions and address them. An extra three minutes now may save you hours of misunderstandings later.

name: Feel Your Feelings
lead: Sometimes, the way to get past something is to go through it
text: Allow yourself to be happy, sad, or angry. Feel your feelings.

name: Happy Place
lead: Where do you feel happy?
text: And safe? Where can you relax and let go? These can be physical or mental spaces. Write them down, have them handy, and visit them often!

name: Play to Learn
lead: If you play to win and you lose, it's not fun
text: But if you play to learn, you always win. Whatever the game, play to learn. And have fun while you do it. This applies to all areas of life.

name: Gratitude Rock
lead: Gratitude keeps you grounded and centered
text: Carry a gratitude rock with you in your pocket or purse. Every time you touch it, stop and think of something you are grateful for. Have a gratitude attitude.

name: No Wrong Taste
lead: Taste varies; objective standards don't
text: Instead of saying something is wrong, say what you prefer. This leaves room for creativity and other opinions. Don't confuse opinions with facts. Facts are universal; opinions are personal.

name: Say Less
lead: Say less than necessary
text: We have two ears and one mouth. Use them proportionally. Talk one third, listen two thirds. When you listen, you learn. And ask questions.

name: Parked Car Theory
lead: You can't learn to drive in a parked car
text: The best way to learn is to do. Start now and figure it out as you go.

name: Get Physical
lead: Physical touch is powerful
text: It grounds you. Grab a book or magazine. Or pick up and feel a stone or a leaf.

name: Process vs Outcome
lead: You can't always control the outcome
text: There may be factors beyond your control. But you can always control your process. Focus on the process rather than the outcome.

name: Clear the Page
lead: The simplest way to clarify your thinking
text: Write a full page about whatever you're dealing with and then delete everything except the 1-2 sentences that explain it best.

name: Lengthen Your Timeline
lead: Hofstadter's Law: things always take longer than you think
text: And even when you take the law into account, you're still surprised. When in doubt, plan more time.

name: Pen Pal
lead: Choose your pen pal
text: Choose a friend or family member and send them a handwritten letter once a month. After 12 letters, exchange the letters to have your personal diary entries.

name: Shun Shouting
lead: When you're having a heated conversation, refrain from shouting
text: Shouting rarely improves the communication. Instead, talk in a soft and friendly voice.

name: Minor Major Repair
lead: If your relationship has a minor issue, repair it
text: Minor issues become major issues over time. Address those swiftly. They won't repair themselves.

name: 10 Year Letter
lead: Write a letter to yourself in ten years
text: What do you hope to have learned, experienced or accomplished? Write it by hand and give it to a friend you trust. Ask them to keep it and return it to you in ten years. Ideally, your friend writes one too, and you swap back. You'll be surprised how much has come true.

name: Zoom Out Doubt
lead: When in doubt, zoom out
text: Struggles can seem larger and growth smaller than they truly are. Zoom out to gain perspective, to see the entire map. Still can't see it? Zoom out further.

name: Feel Good Actions
lead: Which actions reliably always bring you joy?
text: Do you have a song that lifts your mood? Do you feel better after cleaning your room? Make a list of all your feel good actions. And whenever you don't feel great, do one thing from that list!

name: Say Hello
lead: A random interaction can lead to a beautiful relationship
text: You never know what a simple hello can do. Always say hello!

name: Date Yourself
lead: Learn to be by yourself
text: To enjoy your own company. Schedule time for yourself. Simply be.

name: Walk the Way
lead: In order to get ahead with anything, you have to start
text: The Persian poet Rumi says "As you start to walk on the way, the path appears." Trust the process.

name: Optimists' Obstacles
lead: Optimism isn't about ignoring obstacles
text: It's about viewing every obstacle as an opportunity rather than a permanent roadblock. You get rewarded for the number of obstacles that you successfully navigate around. You get rewarded even more if the solution is creative and sustainable.

name: Principle Glue
lead: Write down your principles and stick to them like glue
text: This ensures that what you say and do aligns with what you believe. It also makes you reliable to others and, most importantly, to yourself.

name: Winner/Loser Game
lead: Which game are you playing?
text: Amateur tennis is a Loser's Game. Most points are lost due to unforced errors. You win by avoiding mistakes and waiting for your opponent to make mistakes. Professional tennis is a Winner's Game. Most points are won through making great shots. In any situation, ask yourself: are you better off avoiding mistakes, or is it crucial to bring your A-game?

name: 100 Not 1
lead: Stuck on a problem and can't come up with a single solution?
text: Try coming up with 100 solutions. Write down as many ideas as you can. The act of writing will get your creative juices flowing. Eventually you'll come up with something useful.

name: Be Helpful
lead: Try to be helpful — as a parent, spouse, child, sibling, friend, or leader
text: Share and provide value. Not for some end, but as an end in itself. Being helpful to others is almost always incredibly rewarding!

name: Give Good News
lead: Good news can lift your mood instantly
text: Try to read and spread good news every day!

name: 30-for-30
lead: If you want to make progress, do something for 30 minutes a day, 30 straight days
text: Intensity + Consistency = Progress.

name: Problem or Fact
lead: Is it a problem or a fact?
text: Your height is a fact. You can't change it. Being busy is a problem. You can rearrange your schedule. Solve problems, accept facts.

name: Dry Ships
lead: Ships don't sink because of the water around them
text: Ships sink because of the water that gets in them. Don't let what's happening around you get inside you and weigh you down. Keep your ship dry!

name: Better Breaks
lead: Three ways to have better breaks
text: Moving beats stationary. Outside beats inside. Social beats solo. So, move your body, get some fresh air and interact with others!

name: One Minute Focus
lead: Staring at something for a short time can improve mental focus
text: The next time you need to refocus, take a minute and concentrate on one spot. Or just close your eyes.

name: Don't Add, Subtract
lead: When something isn't working, try subtracting instead of adding
text: Usually, the solution is found by removing something that is holding us back, not by adding something new.

name: Shoshin
lead: Japanese concept from Zen Buddhism meaning "beginner's mind"
text: When learning or working, develop an attitude of openness and eagerness. Let go of any preconceptions. This is how you keep learning, even at an advanced level.

name: "Too Hard" Pile
lead: A way to handle problems
text: Put problems you currently can't solve on a "too hard" pile. Solve easier problems instead, to start generating momentum. Eventually you'll be able to tackle the harder problems.

name: Ordinary Love
lead: Fall in love with the ordinary
text: An amazing life is built through tiny, ordinary, everyday things. Get comfortable with the ordinary, and you'll build the life of your dreams. The quality of your life is determined by the quality of your average Tuesday afternoon.

name: Barber Bias
lead: Don't ask the barber if you need a haircut
text: When seeking someone's advice or opinion, ensure they have your best interests at heart. Of course, there are great barbers who will honestly tell you if you don't need a haircut.

name: Leave the House
lead: If you want change to happen, leave the house
text: Nothing will happen until you step out of your house or leave your current comfort zone.

name: Find Green Flags
lead: When meeting someone new, look for green flags
text: Ask yourself, what do I like about that person? This will make you more open and your interactions more pleasant.

name: Hope vs Expectations
lead: They're not the same
text: Hope can fuel us, and it can be refilled. It opens the door to possibility. Expectations, however, are a trap. They can lead to disappointment. Raise your hopes and lower your expectations to establish a resilient way forward.

name: "Right" Now
lead: There is no "right moment" for a big decision
text: Do the work to make the leap of faith as comfortable as possible. And then open the door, jump out of the plane, and trust that you packed the parachute tight.

name: Easy Is Hard
lead: It's hard to make things easy
text: But it's always worth it. For example, the better the recipe the easier it is to follow. Do the hard work of making things easy. For yourself and for others.

name: Persuasion Paradox
lead: Persuasive people don't argue
text: They observe, listen, and ask thoughtful questions. Argue less, persuade more.

name: No Yes No
lead: Asking yes or no questions can kill conversations before they even begin
text: Ask open-ended questions. They unlock the door to deeper connections.

name: Write a Speech
lead: If you have an important topic to discuss with someone, write a speech
text: A speech forces you to distill your main points. To formulate them clearly. And by making them clear for others, they become clearer for you…

name: Advice Paradox
lead: Beware of more
text: More advice can lead to less clarity. Most advice is well intended, but it might not be right for you. It's dangerous to use someone else's map of reality to navigate your reality. Develop filters. Implement advice selectively. Take the signal, skip the noise.

name: Don't Drink Calories
lead: If you want to lose weight, don't drink your calories
text: It's easier to consume calories by drinking than by eating. Instead of sodas, choose water. Save your calories for eating!

name: Speak Up
lead: The Abilene Paradox occurs when everyone in a group does something no one wants to do
text: Each person thinks they are the only one who objects and doesn't want to rock the boat by speaking up. When in doubt, speak out. Chances are, others may feel the same.

name: 12 Birthdays
lead: Call loved ones or friends every month on the day of their birthday
text: If your friend's birthday is on January 7th, call them every month on the 7th. It's like a mini-birthday, and it's a nice reminder to catch up regularly!

name: Replacement Therapy
lead: Question your beliefs
text: Question your beliefs and try to come up with the opposite. This will help you see things from a different perspective. For instance, if you believe your friend is selfish, try to recall an instance where they acted selflessly.

name: Intense Interest
lead: If you want to be great, you've got to be interested
text: You can force yourself to be fairly good at a lot of things. However, it's impossible to be great at anything if you don't have an intense interest. Most people focus too much on being interesting and not enough on being interested. Being interested is how you become interesting.

name: Real or Imagined
lead: Always ask yourself
text: For each headache, ask yourself: 'Is this mostly real or mostly imagined?' Solve the real problems, release the imagined ones. Worrying about what most people think of you is mostly imagined. Worrying about your upcoming test or exam is real. Go study!

name: Best Me Me
lead: Always be yourself
text: Being yourself is the best thing you can be. Only you can be the best version of yourself. Discover what makes you uniquely you and double down on that. What's the unique gift you bring to the world? No one will ever be better at being you than you.

name: Unproductive Walks
lead: Unproductive walks are the most productive activity
text: No one has ever changed their life by listening to a podcast on 2x speed. You'll generate more life-changing ideas on silent walks without your phone than at a desk with all the productivity tools in the world.

name: Doing Nothing Person
lead: Find someone who you love doing nothing with
text: Life isn't the glamorous, photo-worthy moments. Life is mostly just sitting around doing nothing. When you find the person you love doing nothing with, you've found your life person.

name: What's Right?
lead: Look for what's right...
text: What's wrong is always available, but so is what's right. The more you focus on the good, the more you will see it!

name: Something > Nothing
lead: Doing something is better than doing nothing
text: Five minutes of exercise is better than no exercise at all. Before you do nothing, do something. Anything. No matter how small.

name: Wisdom Compounds
lead: Every day, try to be a little wiser than you were when you woke up
text: Small things become big things. Live as if you were to die tomorrow. Learn as if you were to live forever.

name: Gut Life
lead: Listen to your gut
text: Your gut is the largest advisor for your brain. It collects information about our nutrients but also our cells. Listen to and trust your gut. It knows more than you think!

name: Live to Get
lead: To get what you want, you must first deserve it
text: Want to find a good partner? Start by deserving a good partner. Make a list of all the qualities you're looking for. Then, work on living them. It's hard to attract qualities that you don't have. Similarly, as a parent, it's hard to teach a child values that you don't live by.

name: Second Arrow
lead: The second arrow is optional...
text: We all encounter negative events in our lives, the first arrow. They hit and hurt, and we can't avoid them. But being struck by a second arrow (our reaction to the first) is our choice. Pain is inevitable. Suffering is optional.

name: Magic Three
lead: Use the Rule of Three to communicate clearly
text: When explaining something, make no more than three points. Explain difficult ideas in three ways and make important points three times. When in doubt, go with three: Three points, three ways, three times.

name: Unafraid & Spontaneous
lead: Children are unafraid and spontaneous
text: Adults teach fear. Don't climb that tree. Don't jump from there. Unlearn fear, in a safe way. (Most things are safer than you think). Be unafraid. Be spontaneous. Be more like a child. Like children, you'll have fun and learn a ton!

name: Right or Different
lead: After every experience, (successful or not successful) stop, and replay the situation
text: Ask yourself (on paper): what did I do right? And what would I do different? Reflecting on right makes you better at those things. Reflecting on different lets you see all kinds of possibilities. Answering both is positive and constructive. Try it for one day or one experience.

name: Why Worry
lead: Ask yourself: Do you have a problem in life?
text: If the answer is no, why worry? And if the answer is yes, ask yourself, can you solve it? If you can't, then why worry? And if you can solve it, why worry!? We suffer more in our minds than in reality.

name: Inverse Paranoid
lead: Paranoids are convinced there's a conspiracy against them
text: Be the opposite. Imagine the world is conspiring to help you. And serve you. The next time something you don't like happens, stop. Tell yourself, there must be something good that's going to come out of this.

name: Practice Patience
lead: Patience is a virtue
text: Patience helps you enjoy the present moment rather than rushing off to the next thing. It can also reduce stress levels. When you're patient you're less likely to experience frustrations. And you'll enjoy what you're doing more. The patient gardener will always enjoy gardening more than the impatient one.

name: Invert It
lead: Complex problems are sometimes better solved backwards
text: Turn your next problem or situation upside down. Ask yourself: What do I not want to happen? What could go wrong? Then, work on avoiding that.

name: End of Movie
lead: Imagine watching the last 10 minutes of a movie, knowing how everything turns out
text: Now, if you rewatch the movie, you're relaxed. There's no tension. No matter what happens, you already know the situation resolves itself. Use this in your life. Imagine how a situation turns out. Paint a vivid picture in your head. The more you do it, the more self-confidence you'll experience. And more things in your life will turn out as you expect. Or better!

name: Capability Gap
lead: Ask yourself, what are you capable of and what are you actually doing?
text: People underestimate their full capability and overestimate their current delivery. They think their gap is small, when in reality it's larger than they realise. Ask mentors, friends, and family members to help you see your full capability. And keep you honest on your current level of delivery. Close that gap!

name: Feed Your Mind
lead: You are what you eat (and what you think about)
text: Just as you become what you eat you also become what you think about. If you eat unhealthy food you will lose your health. If you think about sad things, you will feel sad. Feed your mind with positive thoughts. Focus on the good, like a beautiful flower on the side walk for example.

name: Different Not Harder
lead: You're more likely to make a big leap by trying different than by trying harder
text: You can work 10% harder, but a different approach might work 10x better. Persistence is not only about effort, but also strategy. Don't just try harder, try different!

name: Ho'oponopono
lead: A Hawaiian mantra to cleanse the mind
text: Simply repeat these four phrases: "I'm sorry" (acceptance), "Please forgive me" (forgiveness), "Thank you" (gratitude) and "I love you" (love). It has been used for generations to heal relationships, with others and with yourself.

name: Happiness Pillars
lead: Build happiness on family, friends, work, faith
text: You need close ties to family and friends. And you need something to believe in. (This can also be principles). And you also need something to spend your time doing. It doesn't have to be a job that pays. It can be something like tending to your garden.

name: Simplify
lead: Whenever possible, simplify
text: What can be done in three steps should not be done in four. Each link in the chain is a chance to mess things up. Fewer links mean fewer chances for a mess-up.

name: 3AM Friend
lead: Who is your 3 AM friend...?
text: That friend you can call in the middle of the night. That friend who not only answers the phone but you can hear them getting dressed in the background because they are getting ready to be there for you, whatever you need. Some friends you can call sometimes. Who can you call at any time!?

name: Band-Aid Principle
lead: Pull it off fast!
text: The faster you pull off a band-aid, the less it will hurt. Some things in life will hurt. And sometimes there is no way around them. If you know it will hurt, it's better to get it over with fast.

name: You Are Beautiful
lead: Remember, you are beautiful
text: Remember that you are beautiful. We tend to be our greatest critic. Ask yourself: what is the most beautiful thing you know to be true about yourself?

name: Ostrich Effect
lead: Don't be an ostrich
text: While it's a myth that ostriches bury their head in the sand to avoid danger, the idea serves as a metaphor. Just because you're looking away, doesn't mean the danger isn't there. If things are hard or dangerous, open your eyes. Recognise reality, especially when you don't like it. It's important. You cannot solve (or avoid) things you ignore.

name: Choose Your Bucket
lead: If you throw a bucket of water on a small campfire, you'll put it out
text: But, try using that bucket to refill a dried-out lake; not much will happen. Everything is relative. If you invest 8 h in a 10 h project, you'll fail. Put those 10 h into a 6 h project, and you'll likely exceed all expectations. Pick the right size bucket for the problem you're trying to solve. Choose your bucket, choose your future.

name: Rogue Bees
lead: Bees use the waggle dance to show the hive where food is, but some bees go rogue
text: They ignore the waggle and fly off on their own. It's the rogue bees that ensure the survival of the hive; they find new food sources. Without them, the hive would, at some point, deplete their local food sources and die. The lesson: Ignore the waggle around you for a bit. Go out and explore!

name: Green Car Theory
lead: Keep your eyes on the prize
text: Look for opportunities and they will come. Ask yourself, how many green cars did you see today? You probably don't know. Now imagine someone gave you $50 for every green car you see. You would not only notice green cars, you'd actively look for them. Start focusing on the things you want and you will see opportunities everywhere.

name: Piojito Power
lead: Piojito is Spanish for “little louse”
text: To give piojito in Spanish means to gently scratch a loved one's scalp, as if relieving it of the itching of imaginary lice. The stroking activates special nerves in the skin that feel good, reduce pain and lower the heart rate. Receiving piojito relaxes you and helps you bond with the person caressing you.

name: Hand Hugs
lead: How to give a hand hug
text: Hand hug by putting your palm together with another person's palm. Then each person's thumb hugs the other person's hand. It's a cute alternative to interact which is not as intimate and close as a hug.

name: Sour Grapes
lead: A fox wants to eat a bunch of grapes hanging high on a vine
text: Despite his best efforts, he cannot reach them. Finally he gives up, saying the grapes must be sour anyway. The parable highlights the tendency to rationalize and belittle things we cannot get. Beware of sour grapes …

name: Second Mistake
lead: Avoid the second mistake
text: The second mistake is the avoidable one. And the one that usually causes real trouble. When the first mistake breaks our rhythm, we're far more likely to make the second one. It's almost impossible to avoid making a mistake. But avoiding the second mistake is a learnable skill.

name: Never Always Everyone
lead: How often are absolute statements actually true?
text: “You never do the dishes,” “Everyone knows ___,” “I take care of everything in our house...” — very rarely. Instead of being general, be specific. You could say, "The last three times we had dinner, I did the dishes by myself. Would you be willing to help me with the dishes today?"

name: Bigger Risk Question
lead: Ask yourself, what's the bigger risk: going on a new adventure or continuing the adventure you're already on?
text: Sometimes we are afraid of change, but we don't realise that not changing may actually be a greater risk. Not letting go of that relationship that's not serving you may be a greater risk than just moving on.

name: Diving Board Rule
lead: Go step by step and when you're at the edge, jump
text: Remember the first time you jumped from a diving board? You were probably afraid. But all you had to do was put one foot in front of the other and then jump. Next time you want to do something, but you're afraid, think of the diving board. Take it step by step and at the end, jump. But please remember, always be safe!

name: Happy Ten
lead: Count to ten using both hands
text: List 10 things that make you happy, one thing on each finger. This will get you out of your head and back to the present moment. It also reminds you of the things and experiences that make you happy.

name: Be an Amateur
lead: 'Amateur' comes from the Latin word 'amare', which means to love
text: Find things you do for the love of it. Not for some benefit, but for itself. Things you do whether it succeeds or not, whether you are praised for it or not, whether you are loved and rewarded for it or not. Pick up knitting, or painting or something you've always wanted to do. Just be an amateur.

name: Blessing
lead: Count your blessings, not your contributions
text: If you count contributions with your partner, you will never balance the equation. You're comparing apples to oranges to avocados to watermelons. Working for 12 hours and bringing out the trash for three weeks doesn't compare. If you want to count something, count your blessings!

name: C32T Rule
lead: Chew thirty-two times
text: The more you chew, the better you digest. Chewing more can help with weight loss. It helps you break down the food in your mouth, and you feel full faster. Studies suggest chewing 32 times before you swallow your food. That may sound like a lot, but count how often you chew and start by doubling that.

name: Learn the Lesson
lead: You have to live with your mistakes, but you don't have to compound them
text: If you follow up an error with a foolish reaction, you lose twice. Imagine you're cooking and you oversalt the pasta. Don't throw out the entire dish. Ask yourself: Given the reality of where you are right now, what is the best next action? A wise response may not erase a dumb mistake, but it can redeem it.

name: Barber's Back Mirror
lead: Sometimes you need a back mirror
text: Some things in life you cannot see by yourself. After finishing a haircut, the barber holds up a mirror to show the back of your head. It's the only way for you to see it. Sometimes, we need other people's help to show us what we can't see. Who in your life helps you see the things that you can't see? Reach out to them; thank them!

name: Do Hard Things
lead: Deliberately do hard things
text: Practice doing things that challenge you. This way, you keep growing. If you go to the gym and use the same weights every time, your muscles won't grow. But if you always add a bit extra, they will. You also build confidence that you can always do a bit more. Keep challenging yourself to keep growing by doing hard things. Because the hard things eventually become easy.

name: Better Normal
lead: Forget about being the best or exceptional
text: Simply focus on being reliable in the normal moments. Show up when it's easy to skip. Do the basics and do them well. Before you make it complicated, remember there are always simple improvements waiting to be made. Instead of baking the best banana bread ever, just start baking.

name: Prepare to Relax
lead: Gotta be prepared to be relaxed
text: If you want to be relaxed, be prepared. Imagine you're hosting a dinner for your friends. The better prepared you are, the more relaxed you'll be. This is true for most things in life.

name: Create Doorknobs
lead: Doorknobs are questions or statements that encourage the other person to walk through them with a story
text: Create doorknobs in conversations.

name: Walk It Off
lead: When angry, sad or frustrated, walk it off
text: Going for a walk will not solve all your problems. But no problem has ever gotten worse by going for a walk.

name: Listen Loudly
lead: Be a loud listener
text: Show the speaker you are listening with sounds, facial expressions and body language. It shows appreciation and helps you listen at the same time.

name: Find the Issue
lead: Discover what's wrong
text: To start defining your problems, say (out loud) “everything in my life is completely fine.” Notice what objections arise.

name: Daily One
lead: Do one thing every day
text: Collect one stone. Write one word. Take one photo. Sing one song. Pick one flower. Choose one small thing that only takes a few minutes or seconds and do that every day. This will make you more creative. And it will make you happy every day.

name: History Me
lead: Record time pieces
text: It has never been easier to capture text, sound, or video. Write things down, take photos, or record videos. Document important occasions in your life, as well as everyday events. It will be interesting for future generations to see. Wouldn't you have liked to see your parents or grandparents when they were young?

name: Real or Deal
lead: Is it real or a deal?
text: Make a list of all your friends. Next to each name, write 'real' or 'deal.' Real friendships are relationships where you want nothing from the other but their friendship in itself.

name: Fun Part
lead: Focus on the fun part
text: When you're doing something hard, focus on the fun part. Many people emphasise how difficult something is. They tell themselves writing is hard or running is hard or math is hard. If you want to enjoy things more, find the fun part. Focus on that.

name: Reframe the Problem
lead: If you're stuck on a problem
text: If you're stuck on a problem, reframe it. We're wired to fall in love with our first idea. But our first idea may not be the best. Don't get stuck on your first solution. Reframe the problem to come up with a better solution.

name: End Surprises
lead: Stop being surprised
text: If something surprises you again and again, stop being surprised! What's one thing that keeps surprising you? Decide today that you will no longer be surprised by it.

name: Better Not Perfect
lead: Just start and then iterate
text: We rarely do things perfectly the first time. Everything takes work and iteration. Embrace the opportunity to aim for better rather than perfect. Get it wrong the first time. Then make it better.

name: Stop Doing List
lead: What would you stop doing...?
text: What things would you stop doing if you knew you had only one more year to live? Or if you had all the freedom in the world? Would you stop working late nights? Would you stop being on your phone as much? Would you stop spending time with certain people? Write a list of things you would like to stop doing. Then ask yourself, what would have to happen so I could stop now?

name: Piñata Power
lead: Whatever you do, keep at it
text: When you hit a piñata each individual hit compounds until the candy comes out. You're making invisible progress even if it does not seem like it. Keep swinging - the harder it is to bust it open the bigger the rush once it does crack open.

name: Explain the Problem
lead: If you want to solve a problem start by explaining the problem, even just to yourself
text: Often in the process of laying out a problem, a solution will present itself.

name: Body Language
lead: Listen to your body!
text: What is your body telling you that your words might not? Make it a habit to check in and see how your body is feeling.

name: Home Head
lead: Who to let in
text: Never invite anyone into your head who you wouldn't invite into your home. The next time a random person winds you up, ask yourself, "Would I invite them into my home?" If the answer is no, let it go!

name: Count to Ten
lead: The best way to cool your head
text: When you're angry, count to ten. When you're very angry, count to a hundred. Imagine the consequences of saying what's in your head. Then ask yourself if you still want to say it like that.

name: Eat Then Walk
lead: After eating, take a walk
text: Walking for just two minutes after a meal can improve your blood sugar levels. So after your next meal, take a short walk!

name: Point Ping Pong
lead: Stop unproductive point ping pong
text: Unproductive arguments are like ping pong. Hitting facts back and forth, hoping to win. For productive arguments, move away from making points and winning. Rather, focus on understanding the other person.

name: Err on Age
lead: Go for the classics
text: Read, watch or listen to the classics. They're classics for a reason: they've stood the test of time. They don't have to be ancient, either. If you're not into Shakespeare, read Harry Potter or watch The Godfather. The same applies to furniture, fashion and almost anything else.

name: Tell the Truth
lead: A great, simple rule ...
text: Every question has a right answer: the truth. Never lie. It makes life easier in the long run. This doesn't mean you should tell everyone everything all the time. But when they ask, tell the truth.

name: Surf Around
lead: whenever you like something
text: When you find something you like, surf around. Find your next book in your current book. Read footnotes or the bibliography. See what is mentioned. The same is true for authors, actors, hotels, restaurants or anything. If you discover something you love, see what is related to it or by the same person or organisation.

name: Curious, Not Critical
lead: Ask before you assume
text: Next time you're irritated or angry with someone, take a step back. Don't attack. Don't ask, "What's wrong with you?!" Be curious instead. Ask, "What's behind this?" Often we don't understand because we're missing context. Be curious, not critical.

name: Beat Your Books
lead: Read physical books, and read them intensely
text: Read with a pen in your hand. Write in them. Highlight words. Fold pages. Touch them, feel them, smell them. Make each book truly yours.

name: Make That Call
lead: What is that one call?
text: What's the one call you should be making but haven't? The one you keep pushing ahead of you? Don't overthink. Decide and dial. Keeping things in the back of your head drains your energy. Get it out by getting it done.

name: Junk Rules
lead: Have clear "junk rules"
text: Make clear rules about when to throw out old junk. Once the rules are in place, junk is no longer a problem. "I'll keep this broken stereo for five years in case I learn to fix it" becomes a thing of the past.

name: Stop Reading
lead: The rule of thumb for reading
text: Life is too short to read books you don't enjoy, and there are too many books you might love. The rule of thumb is 100 pages minus your age. If you're 70 and don't love a book 30 pages in, stop reading!

name: Feelings and Needs
lead: Listen to feelings to discover underlying needs
text: Often it's not what is said or done, but what we make of it, that shapes how we experience something. When people do things we don't like, it's often a tragic expression of unmet needs. If your partner says, "You never have time," instead of arguing, ask, "Are you feeling sad because you'd like to spend more time together?"

name: Three Options
lead: There are always three options
text: When something bad happens, you can let it define you, let it destroy you, or use it to get stronger. Say you're practising for an important violin concert and you totally bomb. You can call yourself a failure and stop playing, or you can work extra hard to make sure it never happens again.

name: Make Messages Matter
lead: Sending messages today is easy, fast, and free
text: We can send text, voice, video, and pictures almost instantly across the globe. However, there was a time when phone calls were charged by the minute, and text messages were billed by the number of characters. Sending pictures or videos was not possible. When writing to a loved one, make each word matter. Write as if each word was valuable, because it can be.

name: Mess Up Journal
lead: Keep a failure journal
text: Every time you mess up, write it down and leave two lines free. One month later, write what you learned. Six months later, write what good came out of it. This way, each “mess up” brings gratitude and learning. Say you lose your license for speeding. After a month (or sooner), you may learn that it doesn't pay to speed. After a few months, you may have improved your health because you've taken the bicycle instead of the car.

name: Values Not Opinion
lead: Don't define yourself by your opinions
text: They can't change your mind. Define yourself by your values. Sticking to your values ensures that you are true to yourself. And to what you stand for. Instead of saying I don't like crocodiles, say 'it's important for me to feel safe and I am scared of being bitten by a crocodile.'.

name: (Next) Best Thing
lead: A way to decide
text: Next time you decide something, ask yourself: is this the best or merely the next best option? Decisions range from what to wear or cook to where to live. Sometimes the next best is good enough. But most times, it's not.

name: Just for Fun
lead: Make a list of things you love to do purely for the joy of doing them
text: Do you love to golf or garden? To cook or crochet? Write down as many things as you can think of. Keep expanding the list whenever you find or remember something new. Whenever you have time, take out the list and do something from it.

name: Play Kids Games
lead: with and without kids
text: Play games you loved as a child. Play 'hide and seek' or 'I spy.' Use watercolours and crayons … Or build a castle the next time you're at the beach. Children's games are fully immersive. And sometimes that's what we need. Which games did you play as a child? Play that game today!

name: Think About Dishes
lead: When you're doing the dishes, focus on doing the dishes
text: If your mind wanders while doing them, it'll likely wander when you're doing that next task too. Be present. Be in the moment.

name: Book Question
lead: When you meet someone interesting, ask, 'What's a book that changed your life?' Then, go read that book
text: And ask yourself which book has really impacted you (or your views)?

name: Gravity Problems
lead: Ask yourself, is this a gravity problem?
text: You can't change gravity. Only solve problems you can solve. And accept or even befriend the problems you can't! Don't go against the laws of nature (or the market place).

name: Limits Liberate
lead: When in doubt, less is more
text: Having many good options can make it difficult to choose. Consider the famous jam experiment: a table offered 15 types of strawberry jam. While many people stopped to look, almost no one bought jam. However, when the same table displayed only 3 jams, nearly everyone bought one. Reducing your options can make it easier to decide.

name: Karma Coffee
lead: When you're at a cafe, pay for an extra coffee and tell the barista to give it to someone who needs it
text: This Italian concept helps include people who might not have the money to spare for a coffee. Introduce this idea at your local cafe!

name: Check in Request
lead: Ask others to check in on you
text: Sometimes, we forget to simply ask how someone is doing because we're busy. Just asking, "Are you okay?" or "How are you feeling?" can work wonders. This is true even if the answer is "good," and even more so if the answer is "no."

name: Break the Pattern
lead: We all have patterns we've adopted from our families
text: Things our parents used to do or say. Some of these patterns are positive. Some aren't. Say your mother used to shout when things didn't go her way. Is this something you've adopted? Which patterns do you want to break?

name: Pack Lightly
lead: Pack lightly 🪶
text: When packing a bag or suitcase, keep space. It's easier to open and close, and to find things. And you'll have extra space, just in case. If it's too packed, take things out. Or use a bigger bag!

name: Excuse List
lead: Turn excuses into to-dos...
text: What's something you've been wanting to do for a long time but still haven't? Write down the top excuses for why you haven't done it yet. Maybe you've always wanted to travel to a foreign country... Turn your excuse list into your to-do list.

name: Five Star Service
lead: What it (can) look like ...
text: The next time you're hosting a dinner or party, create a five-star experience for your guests. What is the best experience you can imagine? Fresh fruits? Homemade cookies (still slightly warm)? Special decoration? Help them in and out of their coat. Make their favourite dishes. Buy their favourite drinks. Use your best china … Let your creativity run wild. Go all out. You'll have a blast, and so will they!

name: Own Advice
lead: Take your own advice
text: We love giving advice to others. But do we follow it ourselves? What advice do you often give but don't follow? If you say generosity is important, ask yourself: "Am I always generous?" Lead by actions, not by words.

name: What's Not Said
lead: Say the unsaid
text: Often, it's not the things we say, but the things we don't say, that get us in trouble. If you're running late and a friend starts a long chat, it's better to mention you're in a hurry. Suggest rescheduling instead of trying to be polite and listening without being truly present.

name: Take Naps
lead: Take a nap during the day
text: It revitalises you and gives you energy. Nap for around 20 minutes to boost mental alertness and ensure that it is easy to wake up.

name: Remove Barriers
lead: For closer connections
text: If you want to be close to someone, be close to them. Instead of sitting opposite each other, sit next to each other. There's nothing between you. It's natural, comfortable, and fosters closeness.

name: Ask Ends Doubt
lead: When in doubt, just ask
text: Either you will confirm what you thought or you will clarify what you didn't understand. Also, when you're in a group, if you have a question, the chances are high someone else has that question too.

name: Head Heart Check
lead: When making a decision, think about it logically but also feel it out
text: Only inviting the closest family to a special occasion may make logical sense. But does it feel right? The best decisions are those where both the head and the heart say yes!

name: Yes Therapy
lead: Say yes more often
text: We're never too old to try something new. The more new things you try, the younger you'll feel. The next time you're asked to play a video game with your grandchild, say yes!

name: Learn to Juggle
lead: But first learn how to throw
text: Beginners tend to focus on catching. But the secret to juggling is throwing. Start with one ball, throw and let it drop. Practice this for 20-30 minutes. Then, add a second ball: throw, throw, drop, drop. Focus on getting good at throwing. If you're good at throwing, catching becomes natural. Focusing only on outcomes (catching) can lead to trouble. Get the basics right and the rest becomes a lot easier. This is true for juggling and in life.

name: Life Long Learner
lead: It's never too late to learn new things
text: Learning new things can make your life more wonderful. Learn how to cook! Or how to play an instrument. Or pick up that language you learned in school but have gotten rusty in. Get a book, take a class or ask a friend and have fun learning!

name: Thank Specifically
lead: and then elaborate
text: Thank specifically and elaborate. Be specific about what you are thanking someone for. It makes your 'Thank You' more intentional. When your neighbour offers you a ride, thanking specifically might sound like this: Thank you for picking me up. I don't like taking the train. It's much more fun riding together!

name: Ask, Remember, Use
lead: Ask, what's your name?
text: When you meet someone for the first time, ask for their name. Remember it and use it. This shows appreciation and helps build a connection. It's always nice when someone you just met remembers your name and calls you by it.

name: Carry Gifts
lead: Carry little gifts wherever you go
text: Gifts can be small postcards to write a friendly note, a special stone, a book you love or some other little token of appreciation. The best gifts are the ones you don't expect. Carry gifts whenever you go and create beautiful surprises for others! When was the last time you got a surprise gift? What was it? And how did you feel?

name: Laugh to Learn
lead: Path to learning
text: If you want to learn from your mistakes first laugh at your mistake. Also your best teacher is your last mistake. If you are not willing to learn, no one can help you. If you are determined to learn no one can stop you.

name: Five Senses
lead: See, smell, hear, taste and touch
text: When you're feeling in a funk, mix things up. If you've been in front of a screen the entire day, go outside into nature. Close your eyes and smell the air, touch a tree, or simply listen. Use your senses to connect to yourself. Which sense do you use the least, and why?

name: Jour Fixe
lead: How to meet your friends regularly
text: If you want to see your friends regularly, schedule a recurring meeting. Constantly having to schedule outings, dinners, etc. makes it hard to regularly see people. Create standing events. Have a regular routine. Fix the day. It's the easiest way to get more friend time in your week.

name: Five More
lead: Do just five more...
text: The next time you feel like quitting, do 5 more. 5 more minutes of reading, 5 more pages of writing, or 5 more steps of walking. Then, repeat. Sometimes you can break through and keep going. And if you can't, you've still ended five ahead. Tell yourself you'll quit tomorrow, but not today!

name: Common Ground
lead: Focus on common ground
text: Sometimes it's better to focus on the things you agree on instead of arguing who is right or who is wrong. Build connections, not walls - especially with loved ones and other people you care about.

name: Two Magic Words
lead: Thank you and please
text: The most magical words in any language are "thank you" and "please." They connect, appreciate, and show respect. When you visit a new country or meet someone who speaks a different language, learn those words. Also, make it a point to always say "thank you" and "please" as often as possible. These small words have a large effect!

name: Garden Rule
lead: Success is like a garden
text: No matter how green your garden gets or how beautiful your flowers are, you have to keep tending to it. Keep mowing, watering, trimming and edging. If you don't, the grass will turn brown and the flowers will die.

name: Write That Letter
lead: Don't save the kindest words for the eulogy
text: Say nice things and write them down so the person can look at them. Make it heartfelt. Pour your heart onto the page. A handwritten letter is rare, and that makes it special. Create that special moment for someone today.

name: Nurture Your Fire
lead: Emotions are like campfires
text: For a fire to keep burning, you must keep putting in wood. The more wood you put in, the stronger the fire grows. If you keep thinking about how wonderful your life is, your happiness grows. If you focus on anger, it grows too. Put more wood on the fire you want to grow.

name: No Empty Hands
lead: How to clear the table ...
text: When you get up after a meal, make sure everyone carries at least one item from the table to the kitchen. It's the fastest way to clear the table, and it's communal too!

name: Forgive Four
lead: Forgive these four groups of people
text: The quality of your life is determined by the number of grudges you hold. Forgive these four groups of people: Your parents - They did the best they could with what they had and knew. People from previous relationships - There are always two people responsible for a relationship not working out. Everyone else. Yourself - Most unhappiness comes from the inability to let go of the past. Forgive and let go. This frees you from the past!

name: Pay in Advance
lead: An easy way to commit
text: When you're planning a trip, pay in advance. This ensures that you will take the trip. Paying in advance adds an extra level of commitment. Now there is money on the line!

name: Family Vacations
lead: Plan regular family vacations
text: Travelling together and sharing new experiences tightens existing bonds. It can be as small as a short day or weekend trip or as large as an annual ski trip. Whatever you decide: Plan in advance, pay in advance and create a tradition. Paying in advance ensures that you will take the trip!

name: Look Good Limit
lead: Focus on feeling good, not looking good
text: Trying to "look good" limits your life. So, focus on feeling good, rather than looking good. If you can do both, all the better! Be authentic. Be yourself. Remember: People who mind don't matter. But people who matter don't mind.

name: First or Last?
lead: What's most important right now?
text: Sometimes the first move is the most important. The first step gets you walking. The first sentence gets you writing. The first dish gets you cleaning. Other times, the last move is the most important. The last brick finishes the wall. The last brush stroke finishes the painting. The final signature seals the deal. What do you need to focus on right now? First or last? Do you need to start or finish?

name: Happy List
lead: Write it all down ...
text: Write a list of all the happy things and moments in your life. Go back as far as you can remember. When you're feeling sad, pull up the list. Look how far you've come. How blessed you've been. It will put things into perspective. And when a new "happy thing" happens, add it to the list!

name: Turn Things Off
lead: Build bridges of communication
text: When you get home, instead of turning things on (music, news or television), turn things off. If you create the sound of a vacuum, conversation will take its place.

name: No Dire Decisions
lead: Don't decide when you're sad
text: Sadness can cloud your judgement. You might focus on short-term relief rather than long-term benefits, and miss options and opportunities. Make decisions in a neutral state, so they still stand when things are back to normal. Think of a decision you made when you were sad. Would you make it again?

name: Kind Not Right
lead: It's not always about being right ...
text: A short lesson on kindness … There once was a boy who lived with his grandparents. One day, the boy heard an anti-smoking commercial on the radio. "One puff of a cigarette takes 2 minutes off your life..." the reporter said. The young boy sat down and calculated. Excited, he went to his grandmother, who was a chain smoker. He told her that, according to his calculations, she had taken 12 years off her life by smoking. The boy expected praise for his clever calculations. Instead, his grandmother burst into tears. The boy was puzzled. Gently, his grandfather took him outside and gave him a lesson he'd remember for the rest of his life. He said, "Son, one day you will understand that it's easier to be clever than it is to be kind." Remember, It's easier to be clever than it is to be kind. Choose kindness!

name: Golden Rule
lead: If you want a golden life, live by the golden rule
text: Treat others the way you want to be treated. Not better, not worse. If you want others to be kind to you, be kind to them first. How do you want others to treat you? Are you treating them that way?

name: Public vs Private
lead: Praise in public, critique in private
text: There's a time and a place for everything. When in doubt, do it privately. Only critique the behaviour, not the person. Instead of criticism, offer feedback: explain exactly what the person did and what you would have preferred.

name: Experiences, Not Things
lead: Collect experiences, not things
text: A picnic, a loved one and a sky full of stars. Not lavish, priceless. You are the sum of your experiences. Seek out new ones. Create them, cherish them and share them. When did you last have a priceless experience? And when did you last create one for someone else?

name: Add “Yet”
lead: One word makes your negative thoughts positive
text: If you're learning a new skill and hit a roadblock, don't say, "I can't do it." Say, "I can't do it... yet!" This tiny "yet" reminds you that struggles are temporary. With effort and persistence, you can push through. What's a thought you'd like to add a "yet" to?

name: Respond
lead: Don't react, respond
text: Don't let your initial reaction become your response. Seek clarity first. Be curious; don't assume or allow your emotions to control you. When in doubt, ask: "I understood this. Is that what you meant?" Think about the last time you reacted instead of responding. What was the situation? How did it feel?

name: Reply Relaxed
lead: Don't reply when you're angry
text: When you're angry, you may say things in the heat of the moment. Take a breather, go for a walk, or sleep on it. You won't regret taking time to respond when you're relaxed. The next time you're in a heated situation, how will you respond? What's your "cool-down" strategy?

name: Hollywood You
lead: When in doubt, zoom out
text: We've seen the scene. It's clear what the main character should do: Drive to the airport and confess their love Have that hard conversation Or, grab that exciting opportunity The bird's-eye view offers a unique perspective. It lets you see the landscape around you and the bigger picture. You are the main character in your life. What would the audience (you) be screaming at you to do? Perspective is everything. What insight does the bird's-eye view provide that you're missing on the ground?

name: Seek Small Wins
lead: Seek small wins every day
text: We encounter small wins and small losses every day. For example, getting out of bed immediately instead of hitting snooze. Reacting with kindness instead of anger. Or getting back up to brush your teeth even if you're super exhausted. Turn the little things throughout your day into small wins rather than small losses.

name: Dunning-Kruger Effect
lead: How to beat imposter syndrome
text: Beginners are often overconfident. They make a lot of progress fast. Experts' confidence often drops. They realise what they don't know yet. The more expert you become, the more you may feel like an imposter. Feeling like an imposter may therefore actually be a signal that you're ready.

name: Bad Before Good
lead: Want to have good ideas? Have lots of bad ideas first!
text: If you want to do good work, you'll do a lot of bad work first. Hemingway wrote six hours every day. Most of it was bad. Bad is not fatal, and bad is not bad. Bad is the first step towards good!

name: Yield Gold Now
lead: No matter your age, your golden time is now
text: You'll never be younger than you are right now. The greatest gift is the present. Cherish it. No one knows how much time they get. Treat every day as a special occasion, because it is. Imagine buying fine table wear and using it only once a year. After ten years, you'll have only used it ten times. Create more special occasions. Celebrate more often. Use your best china more often. Good things will yield golden memories, and bad things will yield golden lessons. So, yield gold now!

name: Irritation Signal
lead: A way to understand yourself
text: Think about what irritates you in others. Often, these things have less to do with them and more to do with us. They highlight something about us that we've not yet explored. (Or we may want to explore deeper). Next time you're irritated, ask yourself: What feelings and emotions are being triggered? What needs of mine are not met?

name: Go All-In
lead: Whatever You Do, Go All In
text: Once you decide to do something, give it your all. If you do that, no matter the outcome, you'll never have to wonder "What if I had put in more effort?" Remember: The more you lean in, the more you get out!

name: How to Promise
lead: Advice on how to make promises
text: Be stingy in making promises and generous in keeping them. For instance, only promise to do the dishes if you're definitely going to do them. Also, don't feed yourself only on leftovers. When you say yes to others, make sure you're not saying no to yourself. Keep every promise. It makes you credible. To others and to yourself.

name: Same Page Safety
lead: Knowing always beats assuming
text: If you think something goes without saying, it's usually better to just go ahead and say it anyway. Not everyone shares the same perspective. Say the things that you assume are implied. Best case, you'll clear up any confusion. Worst case, everyone already was on the same page.

name: Enjoy Your Bone
lead: Be happy with what you have
text: A dog finds a bone in a trash can. He grabs it and happily runs home. On the way, he passes a pond. In the water, he sees another dog with a bone. He stops and thinks: Why is that bone so much bigger than mine? He barks and tries to steal the other dog's bone, dropping his bone in the water. Remember: Cherish what you have. If you don't, you may lose it.

name: Let Shells Break
lead: Let the chicken break its shell
text: For a chicken to hatch, it needs to break its shell. If the shell is broken for it, it will die. You may see the chicken struggle, and you may want to help. But helping will kill the chicken. The lesson: sometimes help can hinder growth. Allow others to figure things out for themselves. Give them the chance to learn and grow.

name: Advice to Self
lead: What advice would you give yourself?
text: What advice would you give your younger self? Think about the lessons you've learned and about the lessons you're still learning. If you'd tell your younger self to invest in yourself, ask: Are you currently investing in yourself? If not, why not?

name: Treadmill/Sofa Friends
lead: Treadmill friends vs sofa friends
text: Treadmill Friends - after meeting them you have so much energy, you want to run on a treadmill to calm down. Sofa Friends - after meeting them you feel so drained, you want to lie down and recover. Avoid sofa friends. Double down on treadmill friends.

name: The Third Door
lead: There's always a third door
text: Life is like a nightclub. There's the main door where everyone is queuing. The line is long and you might not get in. There's the backstage door. There's no line but you need special access. And then there's the third door. You go down the alley, climb a wall, jump over a dumpster and enter through the kitchen. Whenever you're going after something, ask yourself: where is the third door?

name: Six Word Memoir
lead: Your story in six words
text: To get to the essence of who you are and what matters most, tell the story of your life in six words. Legend has it that Hemingway won a bet with the six-word story "For sale: baby shoes. Never worn." What's yours?

name: Not What, That!
lead: "What" isn't the point
text: When it comes to working out, the point is not what you do. The point is that you do something every day. Consistency matters! The best workout is the one you're excited enough to do every day. What kind of exercise would you enjoy for the rest of your life?

name: Priority, Not Time
lead: Make your actions reflect your priorities
text: Rephrase 'I don't have the time' to 'It's not a priority,' and think about it again. It's a more accurate reflection. If you say, 'I don't have time to call my loved ones,' you're saying 'Calling my loved ones is not a priority.' Next time you 'Don't have time,' ask yourself, 'Is this a priority'?

name: Accept or Change
lead: If you can't change it, accept it
text: Be calm enough to accept the things you cannot change. Be courageous enough to change the things you can. And be wise enough to know the difference. The sooner you accept a given situation, the sooner you can adapt and grow.

name: Yesterday Is Heavy
lead: Put it down
text: Let go of yesterday's anger, shame or sadness. It weighs on you and takes you out of the present moment. The past is past. It can guide and instruct you, but it doesn't define you, and it doesn't determine your future. If you can change it, change it. If you can't, learn from it and move on.

name: Quality Beats Quantity
lead: More isn't the point. Better is
text: When it comes to food, work and relationships, choose better rather than more. If you want to eat healthily, focus on what you eat rather than how much. When in doubt, opt for better, not more.

name: Build Bus Friendships
lead: Build and cherish bus friendships
text: Lots of people want to ride with you in the limo. What you want is someone who will take the bus with you when the limo breaks down. Real friends are there for you when you have nothing to offer in return. Who are your bus friends? Reach out to them!

name: Think 20 Years
lead: You reap what you sow
text: Ask yourself, 'Which decision today is going to be best for our relationship in 20 years?' Prioritising work over loved ones may seem “right” in the moment, but may not be the best decision in the long run. Examine your relationships and the choices you're making. When in doubt, “Think Twenty Years“.

name: Lollipop Trick
lead: If your solution doesn't work, reframe the problem
text: Canadian police struggled with rowdy clubbers in the streets. They tried closing clubs early and adding police shifts. Nothing worked. Then they handed out free lollipops. With their mouths busy, the clubbers stopped shouting and vandalising. The problem disappeared overnight. When conventional logic doesn't work, reframe the problem.

name: The Feeling After
lead: Focus on the feeling after ...
text: Many things that are good for you feel bad before but great after. For example, an early morning run. Similarly, many things that are not good for you feel great before but terrible after. Like eating ten donuts in one go. Lesson: when in doubt, ask yourself, "How will I feel afterwards?"

name: Sleep Test
lead: Next time you fight ...
text: When you disagree or fight with a partner, don't use logic. Use the sleep test. Ask, who's emotionally more invested? Go with their way. Say we go with my way and you can't sleep tonight. If my way turns out to be wrong, you will have suffered and the decision was wrong. When it's a deadlock, ask who won't be able to sleep tonight. You can often adjust later.

name: Six Blind Mice
lead: and an elephant
text: Six blind mice examine an elephant… The first mouse touches the trunk and says that the elephant is like a snake. The second mouse touches the tusk and says that the elephant is like a spear. The third mouse touches the ear and says that the elephant is like a fan. The fourth mouse touches the leg and says that the elephant is like a tree. The fifth mouse touches the side and says the elephant is like a wall. The sixth mouse touches the tail and says the elephant is like a rope. Each mouse is certain that it is right, and that everyone else is wrong. The lesson: don't attribute to malice, ignorance, or stupidity what can be explained by different information.

name: Only Play
lead: Don't do anything that isn't play
text: If you don't feel good about something, stop. Ask yourself, “am I doing this out of fear, shame, guilt, anger, duty, or obligation?” When we want to make life wonderful for others and ourselves, then even hard work has an element of play in it. At the same time, a fun activity done out of obligation, duty, fear, shame or guilt will lose its joy.

name: Make Two Trips
lead: When in doubt, take two trips
text: If you have the any doubt about being able to carry a load in one trip, do yourself a favour and make two trips. Better to walk back to the car than to drive back to the store because you dropped the eggs.

name: R3 Apology
lead: How to truly apologise
text: When apologising, convey three Rs. Empathise with the other (regret). Don't blame someone else (responsibility). And be willing to fix it (remedy).

name: Bad News First
lead: Always give the bad news first
text: If you have good news and bad news, give the bad news first. People remember how things end more than how they begin. Elevate the ending with good news.

name: Sharing Rule
lead: The sharing rule
text: When two people are sharing, one divides and the other chooses.

name: True Wealth
lead: How to really measure your wealth
text: Measure your wealth by the things in your life that money can't buy. Count the things you wouldn't trade for anything in the world. Think about your health, family, friends or beautiful experiences. This week, make an effort to enjoy at least two sunsets.

name: Action Cures Fear
lead: An ounce of action can cure a ton of fear
text: Stress primarily comes from not taking action on things that you could take actions on. The time you spend being afraid of getting hurt could be spent on taking actions to ensure you don't get hurt.

name: Thank Yourself
lead: Always remember to thank yourself
text: Appreciate the work you have done. And celebrate it.

name: Talk to Strangers
lead: Talk to strangers
text: Make unexpected connections. Make beautiful interruptions in the narrative of your day and theirs. Low-risk openers: ask about their shoes. Or use the dog and baby principle: talk to their dog or baby and see if they want to interact.

name: Family Meals
lead: Schedule one day per week for family meals
text: Make it special. Create a tradition. Maybe everyone tells one story or cooks one dish. Be creative. Make it yours. No distractions, no screens. It's a time to bond and share with your loved ones. Quality beats frequency.

name: Poetry Therapy
lead: Poetry therapy helps you access what is alive in you
text: All you need is a pen, a piece of paper and an open heart. When you're ready, pour your heart onto the page. Don't think, just feel.

name: Help, Hear, Hug
lead: Ask how you can support
text: When someone you love comes to you with a problem, ask: "How can I support you? Do you want advice, a listening ear, or a comforting hug?" If they want to be helped, offer solutions. If they want to be heard, listen attentively. If they want to be hugged, hug them.

name: 100 Hours
lead: If you want to grow, develop or excel in a certain area, 18 minutes is all it takes
text: If you focus for 18 minutes per day you will have spent 100 hours in one year working on a specific habit or skill. Say you want to take up knitting 🧶 Commit to knitting 18 minutes every day. After one year you will have spent 100 hours building that skill and habit.

name: Tonight
lead: If it was tonight, would you still do it?
text: Before you commit to something in the future, ask yourself if you'd also commit if it was tonight. We put things off in the future because it seems far away, but bringing it close shows us how we really feel about it.

name: Three Gates
lead: Before you speak, let your words pass through three gates
text: At the first gate, ask yourself, "Is it true?" At the second gate ask, "Is it necessary?" At the third gate ask, "Is it kind?"

name: 100 No's
lead: No just means no
text: Not more, not less. Reduce your fear of rejection by normalising no. Try to collect 100 nos. Start small: ask for a free coffee at a café. And sometimes, just ask why.

name: Two Wolves
lead: We all have two wolves inside of us
text: Both fear and faith are products of the imagination. The difference is: fear is undirected and grows like weeds, while faith requires intentional choice. Be intentional. Feed faith, not fear.

name: Find the Fun
lead: There is always a way to make anything fun
text: A spoonful of sugar helps the medicine go down. If you've decided to do something, you might as well do it in a fun way. If it's not fun, make it so.

name: Three Decisions
lead: The quality of your life depends on three decisions
text: What are you focusing on? What does it mean? What are you going to do now? Say you get a flat tyre 20 minutes into a family road trip. Is it a tragedy because you're delayed, or a blessing because everyone is safe? Do you let anger ruin the day, or turn it into an adventure? The choice is always yours.

name: 5 Year Future
lead: Write down your perfect day 5 years from today
text: Write down exactly what your perfect day would look like. Don't hold back. Write in as much detail as possible. Revisit your writing once a year. You'll be surprised by how much will have come true.

name: Positive Gossip
lead: Compliment people behind their back; it will come back to you
text: Whenever you feel like gossiping, gossip positively. If you talk about other people behind their back, talk only positively about them.

name: Find the Bone
lead: Dogs find bones by searching in the general area, going zigzag until they find them
text: When starting something new, explore the area, go zigzag until you find what you are looking for, and then narrow in.

name: Feed Ducks
lead: Who's happier: the kid or the ducks?
text: When you see a kid feeding ducks, it's hard to know who's happier. Find things in life where giving is just as satisfying as receiving. Feed more ducks.

name: Love to Finish
lead: Fall in love with the art of finishing
text: Falling in love with starting is easy. Falling in love with finishing is hard. Fall in love with the art of finishing — and the process of overcoming adversity, failures and working around obstacles — and you'll consistently follow through on your ideas.

name: What's Enough
lead: What's your definition of "enough"?
text: If you tell yourself you'll be happy when..., you'll never be happy. The finish line will keep moving. Define your place of "enough" and reach it. When you can say, "What I have is good, and everything else is extra," your life will be amazing.

name: Love Sandwich
lead: Offer love sandwiches
text: Deliver a piece of constructive criticism between two tasty slices of positive feedback.

name: Get To
lead: Replace "have to" with "get to"
text: Trade expectation for appreciation and life changes in an instant. Think of all the things you take for granted every day, the things you would miss if they were gone. Be grateful in the moment.

name: Read
lead: Especially in biographies, you get the wisdom of a lifetime in a few hundred pages
text: Seek out great books and biographies to increase your learning.

name: Be an Eagle
lead: When life is challenging you, go higher
text: The only bird that dares to challenge the eagle is the crow. The crow sits on the back of the eagle and pecks at it. The eagle does not respond though. It simply flies higher. At some point it becomes too hard for the crow to breathe. It then jumps off.

name: Drink Tea
lead: Black, green and oolong teas are loaded with antioxidants
text: Tea is good for your heart, brain and focus, and even your mood. Tea is healthy, and exploring different teas is fun.

name: Paradox of Choice
lead: The more choices we have the less likely we are to pursue any option
text: More choice often leads to less action. The more ideas and goals we pursue, the less likely we'll follow through on any one of them. And vice versa.

name: Best Friend
lead: Be your own best friend
text: You are always with yourself. Get to know yourself deeply. Spend time alone. Only once you love yourself can you be your best version and show up in the best possible way for others.

name: I Don't
lead: Say “I don't” instead of “I can't”
text: A simple way to remove any negative habit from your life. “Don't” is a choice. It's empowering. It's your identity. “Can't” is restrictive. It makes you a victim of circumstance. “I don't” changes your brain, which changes your beliefs, which changes your behaviour. Your brain believes what you tell it most, so tell it things that serve you.

name: Buy a Ticket
lead: You can't win if you don't have a ticket
text: A poor man goes to church every day and prays before the statue of a great saint, begging, "Dear saint-please, please, please...give me the grace to win the lottery." This goes on for months. Finally, the statue comes to life, looks down at the begging man and says, "My son-please, please, please...buy a ticket." You cannot win a game you're not playing.

name: Simple Not Easy
lead: Most things in life are simple (but not easy)
text: Losing weight is simple. There are countless, proven step by step guides. Making yourself do it is hard. No one feels like going on a diet - you need to force yourself. Do the hard part of following the simple steps.

name: Life Stories
lead: How to remember the most beautiful things in your life
text: Every night before you sleep, take five minutes to write down the best story of your day. Just jot down key words. At first they may not be very good. Keep going. Trust the process.
