With time you'll sharpen your storyteller lens. Store more memories. And you will have hundreds of stories at the end of each year.

name: Flip M
lead: Replace "Me" with "We" to change your world
text: In relationships, approach a fight as a team. Shift an argument to a shared goal. When fighting as a team, you crush the problem, not your partner. Your partner is not your opponent. Every time one of you loses, you both lose. Every time the problem loses, you both win.

name: Greenlights
lead: Greenlights mean go, advance, continue
text: Greenlights symbolise affirmation, support, and success in our lives. They align with our desires and enable us to move forward with ease. Sometimes they are disguised as yellow and red lights. They appear as obstacles or challenges, but they can provide valuable lessons and give us what we need. Red and yellow lights eventually turn green in the rearview mirror. Catching greenlights involves skill, timing, and adaptability. By identifying and overcoming obstacles, we can create our own greenlights through hard work, smart choices, and resilience.

name: 300 Things
lead: Write down 300 things you desire
text: You will struggle when you get to 70 things. Don't stop until you have 300. Read them every day. Be specific. A year from now you'll have at least 30 of them. Ask and you shall receive. And be clear.

name: Think, Wait, Fast
lead: "I can think. I can wait. I can fast."
text: Think: turn daydreams into achievable goals. Wait: big goals take time and patience. Fast: go without for a while, choosing short-term sacrifice for long-term benefit.

name: Right Now List
lead: Trick your inner procrastinator
text: Write down 3 things you need to do right now to get started on your project. Make the tasks extremely easy to prevent your inner procrastinator from objecting. For example: 1) Find doc I was working on 2) Find where I left off 3) write one sentence. Once you get started, it will be easy for you to get going.

name: Four Words
lead: What do you think?
text: This means you value the other person's opinion. You want to hear what they have to say. Keep a scorecard and try and engage as much as possible.

name: No Fish Love
lead: Beware of fish love
text: True love is one of giving, not of receiving. If you take a fish out of the water, kill it and eat it, then you don't love fish - you love yourself. Too much of love is fish love. Remember: you love those to whom you give.

name: Set Don't Say
lead: Keep your goals to yourself
text: Telling someone your goal makes it less likely to happen. The social psychology tricks your mind into thinking it's already done and you're less likely to do it. Your mind mistakes talking for doing. So state your goals in a way that gives no satisfaction. Make sure your mind knows there's work ahead.

name: Tetris Effect
lead: Train your brain to look for positive things
text: When you practice positive habits such as the "doubling effect" or "Gratitude" your brain starts scanning the world for things to be grateful for and the happier you become.

name: 20 Seconds
lead: Make bad behaviour more annoying to do
text: If you don't want to watch television, remove the batteries from the remote control and put them in the other room. Even though it will only take 20 seconds to get them, your brain will be less likely to do it.

name: Give to Gain
lead: You gain respect by giving it
text: Make a short list of things done to you that you hate. Don't do them, ever. Make another list of things done to you that you love. Do them always.

name: Focus Flow
lead: Where focus goes, energy flows
text: When we focus on things we regret, such as failed relationships, family disputes, and setbacks in career and finance, we tend to become more regretful. Conversely, when we focus on the things we are grateful for, a greater sense of happiness tends to pervade our lives.

name: Day One
lead: Focus on Day One instead of one day
text: Turn anything you want to do “one day” into a tiny thing you start today. What tiny thing could you do every day that adds up to you becoming the person you want to be? Read 3 paragraphs, do 3 push-ups, write for 3 minutes. Pick something so simple it almost can't fail. Plan when and where you'll do it, then start today, not one day.

name: Next Five Minutes
lead: Excellence is the next 5 minutes
text: Excellence is not something in the distant future it's now. It's the next conversation, the next interaction, writing a thank you card.

name: Just One Shot
lead: Take only one picture
text: Next time you are taking a picture, take only one. Look for a good shot, take it and get back into the moment. Often it's more about the reminder of the moment.

name: Ichi-Go Ichi-E
lead: Treasure the uniqueness of each moment
text: Cherish every event you take part in. No moment in life can be repeated. Even if the same people meet in the same place, it will never be the same. Each moment is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Ichi-go (one time), ichi-e (one meeting).

name: 'Maybe' Mindset
lead: Almost everything is relative
text: A farmer's horse ran away. “Bad luck,” said his neighbours. “Maybe,” he said. Days later, it returned with a wild horse. “Good luck!” “Maybe.” His son tried to ride the wild horse and broke his leg. “Bad luck!” “Maybe.” The army came. They took every young man to war, except his son. “Good luck!” “Maybe.” You never know what anything means until the story is over.

name: Stonecutter's Credo
lead: Persistence is the key to success
text: A stonecutter strikes the same rock a hundred times. Nothing happens. Then, on the hundred-and-first blow, it breaks. It wasn't the last blow. It was the hundred before it. Progress is often invisible until suddenly it isn't. Keep going.

name: Plan to Fail
lead: Human brains are better at finding problems than solutions
text: We're evolutionary designed to find threats. Don't ask how to have a good marriage. List all the ways you would destroy your marriage and then do the opposite of that.

name: Just One Bite
lead: Have just one bite
text: Try more, eat less. When you don't feel like trying something new, try just one bite. Maybe you find something new that you really like. One bite helps you appreciate and savour the food. It also keeps you from overeating. Don't skip dessert. Instead try everything, but just one bite. Sharing many different bites increases variety and makes it more fun to eat.

name: Three Buckets
lead: Every week has 168 hours (3 buckets of 56 hours)
text: If you work for eight and sleep for eight hours, you only have one bucket left. Decide carefully what you want to do with that bucket.

name: Check Your Shed
lead: Check your SHED: sleep, hydrate, exercise, diet
text: Take care of your SHED every day. 😴 Get enough sleep every night. 💧 Stay hydrated. 🏋️ Move your body, go for a walk. 🍏 Eat healthy.

name: Double Delight
lead: Remembering happy moments recreates happiness
text: Your brain can't tell the difference between visualisation and actual experience. Take one positive experience from the past 24 hours. Spend 2 minutes writing down every detail about that experience. As you remember it, your brain labels it as meaningful and deepens the imprint. It's a double-dose of daily happiness.

name: Black Swan
lead: A big, unexpected event
text: Black swans are surprising because they deviate from what we know. Whatever idea you have or hear, the opposite may also be true. Keep an open mind.

name: Wabi-Sabi
lead: There is beauty in the changing and the imperfect
text: Celebrate imperfection, impermanence, and simplicity. Find beauty in the ordinary and embrace the authenticity of objects and experiences.

name: Grateful Three
lead: Every day, write down three things you're grateful for
text: For 21 days, spend two minutes a day scanning the world for three new things you're grateful for. This activity trains your brain to scan the world in a new pattern. Train yourself to scan for positives, instead of threats.

name: Kind Card
lead: Praise or thank one person every day
text: For 21 days, spend two minutes each morning writing a positive note, email or text. Do it for a different person every day. If you want to feel good, make someone else feel good.

name: Beware of Almost
lead: Only done is done
text: No one gets a commission for a deal they almost closed. Celebrate, but only when everything is done and dusted.

name: Fun Fifteen
lead: Do your favourite cardio for at least 15 min per day
text: Daily 15 min of cardio is like taking an anti-depressant for six months.

name: Fear Fine
lead: Fine is a sign of surrender
text: Fine tells yourself you're OK not having the thing you really want. If you're happy, say you're happy. If you're sad, say you're sad. And do something about it. The odds of you being born were one in 400 trillion. You're not fine, you're fantastic!

name: 3-2-1 Go
lead: Count down from 3 and then do it
text: If you have an instinct to act on a goal, you must physically move within 3 seconds or your brain will kill it. Most ideas are killed before they are ever acted on. Use the energy in the moment to keep it alive. Write a note, schedule a call, book that ticket, whatever it is - act.

name: Rules Beat Choices
lead: Replace choices with rules
text: If your rule is to brush your teeth in the morning, then it does not matter if you don't feel like it. Design simple rules and systems to achieve your goals. Rules leave no room for negotiation. Systems and Rules beat Goals and Choices every day of the week.

name: Kalachakra
lead: Ancient Indian belief, translated as "The Wheel of Life"
text: Everything goes through a cycle of creation, destruction and rebirth. Enjoy the periods of growth while they last (creation). There will always come a period of struggle (destruction). This too shall pass. It's a chance for a new beginning (rebirth).

name: Reasons Reap Results
lead: Give yourself (or others) a good enough reason
text: If you have the right invitation, it's always the right time. Would you say no to an invitation to the White House? If the why is strong enough the how takes care of itself.

name: Shinrin Yoku
lead: Shinrin yoku means bathing in the forest atmosphere
text: Immerse yourself in nature for better mental and physical health. Once a day, go outside and find the nearest bush or tree. Soak up nature using your senses.

name: Don't Assume
lead: Don't assume answers, ask questions first
text: We make assumptions to feel safe. The unknown scares us. So we invent answers. Sometimes, we'd rather have a wrong answer than no answer. Because not knowing feels worse than being wrong.

name: Hara Hachi Bu
lead: Put your chopsticks down when your stomach is 80% full
text: Stop eating before you're full. Your body takes up to 20 minutes to realise it is full. Remaining a little bit hungry also keeps the body from physically falling into a lethargic state.

name: Fear Setting
lead: We suffer more in imagination than in reality
text: Fear Setting in three steps: Define your biggest fear or worst-case scenario. List all possible negative outcomes and ways to prevent or mitigate them. Reflect on the potential benefits of taking action despite the listed risks.

name: Plus Minus Equal +-=
lead: A three-part system for meaningful relationships and continuous learning
text: Plus: learn from someone with more experience than you. Minus: teach someone with less experience than you. Equal: engage and connect with someone with the same experience as you.

name: Barbershop Principle
lead: If you hang around the barbershop long enough, you're going to get a haircut
text: If you keep at it, sooner or later you will succeed. Create and spend time in environments that are conducive to your goals.

name: Faster Horse Fallacy
lead: If I had asked people what they wanted, they would have said faster horses
text: Only because something has “always been this way”, does not make it right. There is value in taking a step back and looking at things from a different perspective. Times are changing. Make sure you understand the change. Don't just jump onto the More-Of-The-Same bandwagon.

name: Power of "And"
lead: Everything before "but" is irrelevant
text: Using "and" instead of "but" gives more direct and constructive feedback. It also validates others' feelings.

name: Example Not Opinion
lead: The world is changed by your example, not your opinion
text: Your opinion of something will not change it. Taking action and leading by example might.

name: Power Position
lead: If you can't handle not eating candy, don't keep any candy in the house
text: Don't put yourself in a bad position. Environment enables or disables. Change your environment to serve you. Put yourself into a position that is powerful. Don't keep candy at the house.

name: Begin Again
lead: There is always a new moment, a fresh start
text: No matter what happens. You always have the chance to begin again. You miss a day of workouts, begin again. You drop the cake you just finished baking, begin again. Did not stick to your New Year's resolution - just begin again. Instead of beating yourself up, simply begin again.

name: Look Up
lead: Remember to look up at the sky every now and then....
text: Take a moment every now and then and just look up at the sky. It's soothing and magical. And it's always possible, wherever you are.

name: Many Small Plates
lead: Serve meals as a variety of small plates
text: Rather than serving an appetiser, main and dessert, serve meals as a variety of small plates. Smaller portion size encourages you to eat less and also helps increase the variety of vitamins and minerals in your diet.

name: Surfer Mentality
lead: When you catch a wave, enjoy it
text: Ride it as far as you can. Always get into the water. You can't catch a wave sitting on the shore. And don't worry about missing a wave. There is always another one coming. Remember that even the biggest wave ends. Enjoy the ride while it lasts.

name: Switching Costs
lead: It costs you to switch attention between tasks
text: Switching between tasks can lead to mental fatigue and you become more prone to errors. When you start something, try to finish. To make it easier, try Time Boxing or the Pomodoro Technique.

name: 3-2-1 Sleep
lead: Remember 3-2-1 for a good night's sleep
text: 3 hours before bed: no more food or alcohol. 2 hours before: no more work. 1 hour before: no more screens. And 0 times pressing snooze when you wake up.

name: Break a Bone
lead: Setbacks heal and make you stronger
text: Someone who never falls stays afraid of falling. Setbacks hurt, but they heal. And what heals often comes back stronger. So don't be afraid to break a proverbial leg.

name: Seven Whys
lead: Ask “why” seven times to get to the root of an issue
text: Sometimes five is enough. For example: Your car won't start. Why? The battery is dead. Why? The alternator isn't working. Why? The alternator belt broke. Why? It was old and never replaced. Why? The car wasn't serviced on schedule. That's the root cause.

name: Tame the Elephant
lead: Buddha said the mind can behave like a wild elephant
text: It can be led astray by our body's desires, like lust, hunger, and pleasure. Meanwhile, our logic is the rider on top, trying to control it. The rider represents our capacity for rational thinking and decision-making.

name: Easy Does It
lead: Ask yourself - what would this look like if it was easy?
text: If you're struggling with a complex question, try an oversimplified answer. And work from there. This question opens your mind to good options you may subconsciously have dismissed.

name: Build a Snowman
lead: If you want to build a snowman, you have to go into the snow
text: It's going to be cold and might be wet but if you want to build a snowman, you need to go outside. There is no such thing as something for nothing.

name: Get Dressed
lead: Sweatpants are a sign of defeat
text: Get dressed in the morning. Even if you're staying at the house. It signals to your body that you're ready for action. How you dress influences how you feel, and how you feel influences how you act.

name: Acknowledge
lead: Remember, no one makes it alone
text: Have a grateful heart and acknowledge those who helped you. We all need a little help in life! Don't forget to acknowledge the people willing to help you.

name: Just Do It
lead: Actions speak louder than words
text: You cannot think yourself towards a result, you must take action.
The time spent thinking could have been time acting.
Whatever it is, don't talk, just do it.

name: Don't Burn Bridges
lead: You'll be surprised how many times you have to cross the same river
text: Do you really want to have to re-build those bridges down the road?

name: Smart not Hard
lead: Work smart, not hard
text: Before you start a task, think about the best way to complete it.

name: Fast or Far
lead: If you want to go fast, go alone
text: If you want to go far, go together.
When you are by yourself you don't need to wait for anyone, but how far will that take you?
If you want to go far, you need others. Being together is also more fun than being alone.

name: One Good Day
lead: Your life is the sum of how you live each day
text: Spend one good day. Go to bed. Do it again. Time magnifies. You can break it down even further: have five good minutes.

name: Learnings List
lead: Keep a "What I learned today" list
text: Whenever you learn something about yourself, others or in general, write it down.
Add the date and the learning in one sentence.
Revisit this regularly.

name: Collect Happy Moments
lead: When something good happens , write it down
text: Keep this list close to you. In a notebook or on your phone.
Whenever you don't feel good, look at the list. It will uplift you.

name: I Love You
lead: Never waste an opportunity to tell someone you love them
text: Tell the people you care about that you love them. It's such a simple gesture, with such a big impact.

name: Substitution Solution
lead: Substitute a bad habit with a good one
text: Breaking a bad habit can be very hard. Instead, substitute the bad habit with a good one.
If we stop something it leaves a hole. In order to not fall back, fill it with something good.

name: Solutions
lead: Focus on the solution, not the problem
text: Be solution conscious.
Don't say “I can't afford this.” Ask yourself, “how can I afford this?”

name: Jerry's Question
lead: How are you complicit in creating the conditions you say you don't want?
text: Observe your behaviour. What are the habits and routines that lead you to be in a position you don't like or want?

name: Input Edge
lead: The edge is in the inputs
text: The person who consumes from better sources, gets better thoughts.
The person who asks better questions, gets better answers.
The person who builds better habits, gets better results.
It's not the outcomes. It's the inputs.

name: Tombstone Tagline
lead: Try this exercise to explore your values
text: Reflect on what you want your tombstone to say at the end of your life— for example “was a loving parent”—and write it down.
Then think about what your tombstone would say if you died in your sleep tonight.
This exercise can be powerful. It shines a light on what you want your life to be about and on the gap that might exist.

name: Donut Danger
lead: Focus on the donut, not the hole
text: Focus on what you have, not on what you're missing.
Most of the time what you have is pretty great, if you choose to see it.

name: Ta-da List
lead: Turn your To-Do list into a Ta-Da list
text: Write down every task as you complete it. Make it pretty - add stickers and doodles!
Rather than an unfinished to-do list, you'll end the day with a list of accomplishments.
We're better at remembering unfinished tasks than completed ones. A Ta-Da List shifts our focus.

name: Love Your Grass
lead: What are the things you can be grateful for or proud of?
text: Sometimes we get into a funk. We feel like the grass is greener on the other side. We think others have it better or easier.
Next time this happens, imagine you're a stranger looking at your “grass”.
What would they like about your grass? You're probably living someone's biggest dream. Focus on yourself. Love your own grass.

name: Seinfeld Strategy
lead: Don't break the chain
text: Get a big wall calendar with the whole year on one page.
Each day you stick to your habit, mark a big X over it. After a few days you'll have a chain.
You'll like seeing that chain, especially after a few weeks. Your only job is to not break the chain.

name: Checklist Charm
lead: Checklists are everywhere
text: From instructions on how to wash your hands to building skyscrapers. A good checklist can help you complete tasks more quickly and efficiently, and with fewer mistakes.

name: Secret Sword
lead: Think twice before burdening a friend with a secret
text: Secrets are dangerous.
When you tell a friend a secret, you've put them in an uncomfortable situation.
Are they really better off knowing the secret than not knowing it?

name: Fish Don't Climb
lead: If you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree, it will live its whole life believing that it is stupid
text: While a bird, a monkey and a fish line up, an official says:
"For a fair selection everybody has to take the same exam: please climb that tree.”
It's foolish to judge everybody by the same metrics, ignoring individual strengths and weaknesses.

name: Make it Matter
lead: Whatever you do, make it matter
text: There is a huge difference between doing things half heartedly and with full effort.
Whatever it is, go all in. Make it matter.

name: Send Flowers
lead: Send your loved ones flowers
text: Think of a reason later.
You don't need a reason to send your loved ones flowers.
It's always a nice surprise.
You can substitute flowers for any other nice surprise.

name: Dead Person's Goals
lead: Goals that a dead person can do better than a living person
text: “I want to stop procrastinating / drink less / care less about what other people think of me…” are dead person goals.
A corpse doesn't procrastinate, drink, or care what others think.
Bring goals to life by asking: “What is doing less of {X} making room for?”

name: Be Graceful
lead: Be a graceful winner (and loser)
text: Be humble in both victory and defeat.
In defeat, congratulate the winner. Let them have their celebration.
In victory, congratulate the losers on their good effort.

name: Morning Music
lead: Begin each day with some of your favourite music
text: Studies show that what we hear within the first 20 minutes of waking up has a big effect on our mood for the rest of the day.
Play your favourite music every morning.

name: First Follower
lead: It's the first follower that turns a “lone nut” into a leader
text: Without the first follower there is no movement.
The best way to start a movement, is to follow and show others how to follow.
When you find a lone nut doing something great, have the guts to be the first person to join in.

name: Eight Minute Call
lead: Call someone you love, miss, and wish you connected with more often
text: Text them and propose an eight minute phone call — ideally today, or sometime this week.
We tend to think that in some unspecified future, we'll have a 'time surplus,' to connect with old friends. However, this may never come. Pick up the phone and invest the time right now.

name: Make Magical Moments
lead: Make magical moments
text: Randomly. Every day.
Magical moments are unexpected acts of kindness.
Cast members at Disneyland are given opportunities to give families a special memory they will never forget.
Magical moments come in all sizes. From giving a child a Mickey sticker, to upgrading your resort hotel room.
✔ Make one magical moment today

name: Yin & Yang
lead: Everything contains the seed of its opposite
text: Yin and yang are opposite but connected forces, like dark and light. In every problem lies a chance, and in every strength a weakness. Look for the other side.

name: Let Go Lending
lead: Only lend things you never care to see again
text: If you have trouble lending things to others, lend only those things that you don't mind not seeing again.
That way you won't be chasing people for them back.
You may also want to make a habit of gifting things.
If someone asks you to borrow a book, gift it.

name: Wu Wei
lead: The Chinese concept of effortless action
text: A river isn't pushed or pulled. It simply flows. Stop forcing things. Get out of your own way. Don't row, sail.

name: Challenge First
lead: The next time you want to buy something, set a challenge first
text: For example, commit to running every single day for a month before buying that new running outfit.
This way you will have something to look forward to.
You will also feel proud and like you've earned it.

name: Veblen Good
lead: A type of luxury good for which the demand increases as the price increases
text: We often attach value to things simply because they're hard to get. People will be more attracted to a $3 million painting than a $3 painting. The price becomes a feature of the product. It allows the buyer to signal affluence to others.

name: Gambler's Fallacy
lead: We often feel we're owed luck for being unlucky
text: "The coin was heads 10 flips in a row, the next flip has gotta be tails!"
But probability has no memory.
It won't make amends for its past behaviour.
Therefore, treat every possibility independent of the past.

name: No Nay Sayers
lead: First they ignore you, then they laugh at you, then they fight you, then you win
text: When zippers began replacing buttons, there were those who resisted the change because they believed zippers were sinful: they made it easier to disrobe.
Even light-bulbs (light at night is not the way God intended!) or mirrors (think of the vanity that will ensue!) were viewed sceptically by some.
There will always be people who won't welcome change.
Don't let that discourage you.

name: Teach to Learn
lead: You only really understand something if you can teach it to someone else
text: If you're learning a new skill, take any opportunity to teach it to someone else.
It's a nice thing to do and it will also improve your learning.

name: Two not Three
lead: Give people a second chance, but not a third
text: Everybody makes mistakes. People deserve a second chance. But if they mess up both chances it's no longer an accidental mistake. It becomes deliberate.

name: North Star
lead: A north star is like an invisible mentor ready to guide you every step of the way
text: Identify 3–5 significant areas of your life. It can be your career, relationships, finances, and others.
Imagine the ideal situation in each of these areas.
With this guideline as your north star for that area of your life, every time you need to make a choice, it's there to guide you towards the right one.

name: Zettelkasten
lead: Zettelkasten (German: "slip box", plural Zettelkästen)
text: A Zettelkasten or card file is a method to manage knowledge.
Take ideas from books, articles or conversations
Write these ideas on note cards
Collect them in a central database (digitally) or a “Zettelkasten“ (physically)
Link them together and start finding larger relationships between concepts you're learning
☝️ This is how the idea for happy habits initially started - our personal Zettelkasten

name: Gratitude Gateway
lead: If you want to be happy, be grateful
text: Think of someone you are grateful for and send them a handwritten letter, text message, voice note or give them a call.
Alternatively, take a moment and think of all the things you are grateful for.

name: Top Three Things
lead: What are the three best things you did today, this week, this month or this year?
text: Ask yourself “What are the best three things you did this year?”
What made them “the best”?
And what can you do to get more of this?
☝️ Take a few minutes to do this now
This method can also be used for things and events in the future.
What are you most looking forward to?
Why are you looking forward to this?
How can you create more of this in your life?

name: The Greatest Illusion
lead: The greatest illusion is that life should be perfect
text: Not everything in life is going to go according to plan, and that is okay.

name: The Greatest Freedom
lead: One of our greatest freedoms is how we react to things
text: It's not what happens to you that matters, but how you respond to it.

name: Measure of Value
lead: Don't measure your value by how you are treated
text: Value yourself and treat yourself how you wish to be treated. Others will follow.

name: Cut Comparing
lead: The biggest waste of time is comparing yourself to others
text: Focus on yourself. You are the only one you can change. Run your race.

name: Ask for Help
lead: Asking for help isn't giving up, it's refusing to give up
text: What's the bravest thing you've ever said? Help.

name: Other People's Mistakes
lead: Learn from the mistakes of others
text: You can't live long enough to make them all yourself.
Most things have been done before.
There are countless books and videos discussing how and why failures occurred.
Before beginning a project, consider whether it's been done before and apply the lessons learned.

name: Build a Strawman
lead: Create a straw man draft and knock it down to rebuild something better
text: The idea behind the “Straw Man” is to create a first draft for criticism and testing.
Use the feedback to develop subsequent iterations to get a rock solid final outcome.

name: Hard Part First
lead: Do the hard part first
text: If the hard part doesn't work, nothing will.
Imagine you want to promote a cheese-juggling mouse on a pedestal.
Don't waste time engineering the pedestal. The hard part is training the mouse.
For any project, ask yourself, what is the hard part? And do that first.

name: Play Backgammon
lead: Backgammon is the game of life
text: Persians say the board is our life and the dice are our fate. You can't always roll double six, and not everything is in your power. Lone checkers are vulnerable. We are stronger together. Do your best, and accept what you can't control.

name: Spin the Spinner
lead: When you have too many options, make a spinner and spin it
text: Sometimes, when there are too many similar choices, choose one and start. It may be easier to reason why you chose that one than it is to choose the “right one“.
Sometimes you just have to start. Spin the spinner.

name: Find a Compass
lead: If you're stuck, find a compass, not a map
text: A map gives you directions from A to B, but a compass will help you find true north wherever you are.
Sometimes we get so wrapped up in the outside world that we don't focus on what we like but on what we'd like to like.
Passion pulls you toward your current interests. Values point you toward a future purpose.
Following your passion is a luxury. Following your values is a necessity.
Passion brings immediate joy. Values give lasting meaning.

name: Parkinson's Law
lead: Work expands so as to fill the time available for its completion
text: If you give yourself five hours to complete a task, it will take you five.
If you only give yourself one hour for the same task, it will only take you one.

name: Good Blocks Great
lead: Don't settle for less just because it's available
text: Think carefully how you want to invest your time.
If you commit to something that is only good you are blocking yourself from being able to do something that is great.

name: The Last Time
lead: If you always do things as if it is the last time, at some point it will be
text: Long before you die, you will stop having certain experiences. Experiences that you take for granted now.

However, you rarely know when you will be doing something for the last time. When is the last time you will go camping? When is the last time you will stay up all night talking to a friend? If you're a parent, when is the last time you will tuck in your child and read a bedtime story?
Cherish those moments because each one of them is priceless.

name: Efficient vs Effective
lead: Do right things before doing things right
text: Efficient means doing things right while effective means doing the right things. First be effective. Only after that optimise for efficiency.

name: Placebo Effect
lead: What you think is what it does
text: A placebo works because you believe it will. It changes the story you tell yourself, and those stories are powerful. They can ease pain, make wine taste better and even grow hair.

name: Hindsight Insight
lead: The most fertile source of insight is hindsight
text: If you want to make better decisions in the future you need to understand the past.
History repeats itself.

name: Four Thousand Weeks
lead: If you live to be eighty, you have just over four thousand weeks
text: How do you want to spend those weeks? With whom? And where?

name: ASAP
lead: As Soon As Possible
text: When someone asks you to do something "As Soon As Possible" - beware.
Before you jump onto the task by focusing on “soon”, take a step back and think about “possible”.

name: Two Pizza Rule
lead: If two pizzas won't do it, try fewer people
text: If you want to achieve anything, the team should be small enough to be fed with two pizzas. Small teams spend less time coordinating and more time doing.

name: Chisoku
lead: Chisoku (Japanese) To feel sufficient
text: To be satisfied with what you have.
Enough is a choice. And choices are deeply personal.
So if you decide you have enough, then you do.

name: Don't Die
lead: All I want to know is where I'm going to die so I'll never go there
text: Sometimes it is more important to know what not to do than to know what to do.

name: Metaphor not Memorisation
lead: Don't memorise, metaphorise
text: If you understand A, and B is like A but a little different, you understand B. Metaphors help you make sense of new things through what you already know.

name: Bound by Big
lead: Narcissism of small differences
text: Don't let differences in little things divide you when agreement on the big things should bind you.

name: Ask, Don't Tell
lead: Those convinced against their will are of the same opinion still
text: Instead of imparting knowledge directly, ask probing, thought-provoking questions.
The Greek philosopher Socrates believed that we hold the answers within us.
We just need to be asked the right questions to expose them.
This is known as the Socratic Method.

name: What Changed?
lead: If it didn't work before, what changed?
text: If you want to do something that has previously not worked, ask yourself:
How is the current situation different? Why do you deviate from the statistics. It's fully possible but you have to think about it.

name: Learning Not Failure
lead: I have not failed
text: I've just found 10,000 ways that won't work.
When you build upon something that has not worked, you have not failed.
Many things in life are trial and error.
As long as you learn you have not failed.

name: Ask Better Questions
lead: The quality of your life is determined by the quality of the questions you ask
text: The better the questions you ask, the better the answers you will receive.
Asking "why can't I lose weight?" is not as empowering as "how can I lose 5KG?"

name: One New Thing
lead: Learn or experience one new thing every week
text: Trying new things gives you a dopamine hit (feel good chemical) and makes you feel rewarded.
Fear is often the biggest barrier to trying new things.
To get around this, start small. Make a plan and prioritise fun.
If you do one new thing every week you'll have done 52 new things in one year.

name: Anything Is Everything
lead: How you do anything is how you do everything
text: In any area of your life this will most probably be true and transferable.
If you pay attention to detail you tend to pay attention to detail in every situation. If you are honest and loyal you tend to be honest and loyal in all areas of your life.

name: Don't Be Crazy
lead: Insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results
text: Learn from your mistakes.
If you have not succeeded with a certain strategy in the past, ask yourself
“What's different, what changed, why should it work now“?
If you don't have a good answer, don't repeat the old strategy again.

name: Handshake Overhead
lead: Fewer is faster
text: Two people need one handshake to get introduced. Nine people need 36. More people means more handshakes. Keep things small. Law of more people: n*(n – 1)/2.

name: 1440 Minutes
lead: Every day you get 1,440 minutes
text: You can't transfer them and you can't save them. Use them or lose them.

name: Road not Wall
lead: In competitive auto racing, they teach drivers to “focus on the road, not the wall.”
text: Look at the wall and you'll crash. To win, you need to keep your eye where you want the car to go.

name: Dr. No
lead: Time is the only thing you cannot get back, spend it wisely
text: Saying NO is the ultimate productivity hack.
There's no faster way to be done with a task than not doing it.

name: Kill Criticism
lead: Stop criticising and praise instead
text: Everyone has a reason for doing things.
In their mind they are doing right, they always have a justification.
Focus on what they are doing well and you will get more of that.

name: Discipline Beats Motivation
lead: Discipline beats motivation every day of the week
text: Discipline is superior to motivation.
The former can be trained, the latter is fleeting.
You won't be able to accomplish great things if you're only relying on motivation.
Discipline will push you through the rainy days, which will undoubtedly come.
Be motivated but stay disciplined.

name: Done Beats Perfect
lead: If you are not embarrassed by the first version of your product, you've launched too late
text: Getting your creation out into the world is more important than getting it perfect.
Actions speak louder than words. So put your words to action.

name: Rise and Shine
lead: Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise
text: A healthy sleep routine improves your mood, health and focus. Aim for 7–9 hours. Keep the same schedule every day, even on weekends. Put your phone away half an hour before bed, and skip caffeine and alcohol in the evening.

name: Horse Rule
lead: If five people call something a donkey, it's not a horse
text: Take a poll of five of your most trusted mentors when making a critical decision. These people will generally lead you to the appropriate outcome.

name: Sleep on It
lead: If you are facing a big decision, take a night and sleep on it
text: Being able to sleep on a decision gives you more time to think about it. However, it also gives you a chance to not think about the issue for a while.
Take time, relax your mind and get rest. When you wake up the next day you can think about the issue again and make a better decision.
Most big decisions don't need to be made in the heat of the moment.

name: Set Expectations
lead: If others know what to expect they can self select
text: If you know the movie is scary people who don't like scary movies will not bother going.
Setting expectations eliminates unpleasant surprises.

name: Repeat to Reassure
lead: Repeat in your own words to avoid miscommunication
text: By repeating what someone said in your own words, you can make sure that what you understood is also what they said and meant.

name: Constant Control
lead: You always have the power to choose how you respond
text: You may be in a situation where you don't control anything.
However, what you always control is how you think and what to do about it.
When something happens that you don't like: Ask yourself, is it really that bad OR how is this a good thing?

name: Know the Truth
lead: You can't change what you don't know
text: "Protecting" people by not telling them the truth is like letting kids grow up still believing in the Tooth Fairy. The truth empowers people to change and grow. You can say anything, as long as you say it kindly and respectfully.

name: First Principles
lead: Break down complicated problems into basic elements and reassemble them from the ground up
text: Ask yourself: what are all the things I know for a fact to be true?
Then reconstruct these building blocks in a more efficient, better way.
Deconstruct then reconstruct.

name: Tell Ten
lead: Tell your idea or concept to ten people
text: If it spreads, it works. If it doesn't, go back to the drawing board. You can also stress test your ideas or plans like this. If the majority point out a certain flaw in your thinking it may be worth exploring it.

name: Skip and Revisit
lead: If something is not going anywhere
text: Stop doing it and revisit it later.

This can be valuable when working on a task that you are stuck on. Rather than wasting time trying to figure it out, move on to the next task. Similarly if you're having a meeting or argument that does not seem to come to a conclusion. Simply suggest to stop and postpone it.
Often a bit of time and a fresh pair of eyes and ears works wonders.

name: Take Shots
lead: You miss 100% of the shots that you don't take
text: Not trying is worse than trying and not succeeding.
Just take a shot.

name: Two Minute Mute
lead: Give someone two uninterrupted minutes to explain their thinking
text: Only after that you can jump in with your thoughts.
This gives people enough time to explain and not be drowned out.

name: Know Your Audience
lead: Think about who you're speaking to and formulate your message accordingly
text: Use your audience as a filter to decide what to say and how to say it.
A Doctor will have to speak differently to his patient than to a colleague.
The patient will be missing the lingo and the background.

name: Time Boxing
lead: Give every task a time box
text: Before you start a task, decide how long you'll spend on it. When the time is up, stop. A time limit keeps you focused, and you'll learn how long things really take.

name: Deep vs Wide
lead: Should you go deep or wide?
text: When you are starting out, go wide. Explore different options.
Find out what you like and what you're good at.
Once you know, go deep.
Focus. Double down on that thing.

name: Pay Yourself First
lead: Rule #1 in The Richest Man in Babylon
text: As soon as money comes in, set aside a fixed amount to save or invest. Treat it like a bill you can't skip. What's left is what you can spend.

name: 5x5 Rule
lead: Most people fail in life because they major in minor things
text: Many people spend a lot of time thinking about unimportant things. Always ask yourself, will this matter in 5 years?
If it doesn't matter in 5 years, don't spend more than 5 minutes thinking about it.

name: Delay Procrastination
lead: Procrastination comes naturally, so apply it to bad things
text: If you feel like binging on fast food, tell yourself you'll do it in an hour.
In an hour, repeat.
Much like our good plans fall apart while we delay them, so do our bad plans.

name: Dr. X
lead: When facing a difficult decision, ask yourself: "Who has successfully dealt with this kind of situation before?"
text: Ask yourself: "What would person X do in my position?"
Better yet, reach out and ask them directly.
If that's not possible, read their books, watch their videos or listen to their talks.

name: Stand, Lay, Spend
lead: If you stand in it or lay in it, spend money on it
text: It makes sense to spend money on good shoes and a good bed and mattress.
If you're not in one you'll be in the other.
Things you use for a significant fraction of your life (for example your bed, 1/3 of your life) are worth investing in.

name: Flea Fallacy
lead: Take off the lid
text: A flea in a jar without a lid will jump out. Put a lid on and it will hit the lid. It learns to stop jumping so high. And even after you remove the lid, it won't jump out. The lid is gone. The limit remains. Don't be a flea and mistake old limits for real ones.

name: Sunk Cost Fallacy
lead: Don't throw good money after bad money
text: Have you ever …📈 continued with a project long after you should have abandoned it? 💔 stayed in a relationship even after the point of no return? 🍿 sat through a bad movie only because you paid for the theatre ticket?
These are examples of the sunk cost fallacy.
The core lesson is that any unrecoverable costs (“sunk” in the past) are irrelevant when deciding what to do next.

name: KISS
lead: If you can't explain it to a six-year-old, you don't understand it well enough
text: It's hard to make things simple.
But simple works best.
(Acronym) Keep It Simple, Stupid.

name: Less but Better
lead: Weniger, aber besser
text: Often less is more. In design but also in life generally.
Better to have one very good handbag than to have five not so good ones.
You will have better service, longer warranty and general durability.
Pursue less but seek better.

name: Be a Shark
lead: If sharks stop swimming, they stop receiving oxygen - don't stop swimming
text: Great white sharks can only breathe by swimming with their mouths open.
The faster they swim, the more water is pushed through their gills.
They swim or they die. Be a shark. Keep on keeping on.

name: Take Chances
lead: Take chances, make mistakes and get messy!
text: In order to learn, you will need to take risks.
You will make mistakes.
And just like little kids growing up and falling down, you can get dirty or messy.

name: Never Eat Alone
lead: Having meals has historically been a communal activity
text: Always try to eat in company of others.
It's a great opportunity to bond and it's nicer that way.

name: Protect the Downside
lead: Trust your instincts, but protect the downside
text: Whatever decision you are facing, think about the downside.
Ask yourself, “what could go wrong?”
If the downside or risk is big, make sure you have it protected.

name: Time Travel
lead: You have a plan
text: A time traveller appears from the future and tells you your plan failed. Which part of your plan do you think is the one that failed? Fix that part.

name: Boomerang Theory
lead: Treat others the way you want to be treated
text: Viciousness you excuse in yourself, friends, or others will one day return to you, and then you won't have an excuse.
Remember, what goes around, comes around.

name: Anything You Want
lead: You can get anything you want if you help other people get what they want
text: The thing you don't enjoy doing, someone else loves to do.
Find those people and let them do it.
Make sure you know what makes you happy, and don't forget it.

name: Give Compliments
lead: Everyone is hungry for compliments, love and appreciation
text: Genuine compliments build relationships, improve communication, motivate people, and boost one's self-esteem and self-confidence.
Give more compliments.

name: Clean Workspace
lead: A workspace is not a place for storing things
text: It's a place for accomplishing things.
Keep your desk and workspace bare.
Treat every object as an imposition upon your attention, because it is.

name: Sturgeon's Law
lead: Ninety-percent of everything is crud
text: Sturgeon's law states that 90% of everything is rubbish.
If you dislike poetry, fine art, or anything, it's possible you've only ever seen "the rubbish version".
Continue looking. The great is rare.

name: Who Not How
lead: Look for "who", not for "how"
text: Instead of asking "How can I achieve this goal?", ask "Who can help me achieve it?" People often get stuck on the how. It's much better to think about who you can team up with. "Who" creates results, "how" creates problems.

name: Skinny Doctor
lead: If you want to lose weight speak to your skinny doctor
text: Only take advice from people who believe in what they are preaching.

name: Live Lucky
lead: Attitude is King, Queen and Head of State
text: Expect the best and good things will happen.
Make a habit of always expecting the best.

name: Be a Child
lead: Carry the spirit of the child
text: Children feel they can do anything they want. And they feel they don't have to do anything they don't want. Be more like a child. Play, experiment and be unafraid (within reason).

name: Rocking Chair Test
lead: Project your life forward to age 90 and take the route that minimises regrets
text: Use the Rocking Chair Test when you have to make an important decision.
Picture yourself sitting in a rocking chair when you're 90 years old looking back upon your life.
Ask yourself "how happy will I be with the decision I am about to make?"

name: Come Prepared
lead: Whatever you do, come prepared for the task
text: If you're called to fix a sink, make sure to bring your tools.
Also make sure that you know what to do and how to do it.

name: Play Your Tape
lead: Practice does not make perfect
text: Only perfect practice makes perfect.
If you're about to give a speech or you are getting ready for an important presentation, practice in your mind.
Practice how you feel, what you think and what you hear. So when it's showtime, all you have to do is play that tape.

name: No Free Lunch
lead: Everything has its price
text: Be sure you know what the price is and if you're willing to pay it.
The things that are "free" might actually be the most expensive after all.

name: Just Good Knives
lead: If you're looking for your "good" knife, you have "bad" knives
text: Throw those out.
What good does a bad knife do?
Keep only the good knives.
Knives stand for anything in your life.
Focus on having less but better things and relationships.

name: Wheels Work
lead: Don't (always) reinvent the wheel
text: Sometimes it's good to look at what is working and to work with and build on that.

name: Time vs Money
lead: You can either invest your time or your money
text: Money comes and money goes. Time only goes. Always keep that in mind when making decisions.
For example, you can either do your laundry yourself or you can pay someone to do it. Ask yourself: how much is not spending the next hour doing laundry worth to me?

name: Power of Now
lead: The present moment is all you have
text: Make now the primary focus of your life.
The only real reality is the moment you are in right now. The next moment never "arrives". Once it does, it is the present moment.
If there is only this moment and you always treat this moment as a means to come to the next moment (not being fully in it) then you are never truly present.
Be present. Live in the "now".

name: Two Millimeter
lead: The smallest changes can yield the biggest results
text: When you're playing golf a 2 millimetre adjustment can make the difference between a perfect shot or the ball going all over the place.
A small improvement made in a few key areas can result in great results.
It's those tiny little habits that add up - a week from now, a month from now, a year from now - to make a profound difference.
The little things matter.

name: Decision Making Fatigue
lead: Automate to eliminate decision making fatigue
text: Every day you have a certain number of “good decisions” in you.
The better you use those, the better the quality of your life will be.
Don't waste your mental energy on making easy decisions.
For instance, lay out your clothes for the next day so you don't have to think about it in the morning.

name: Pomodoro Technique
lead: Work with the time that you have, rather than against it
text: This popular time management method asks you to alternate “pomodoros” (focused work sessions) with frequent short breaks. This sustains concentration for longer.
How to 📝
(1) Pick a task
(2) Set a 25 minute timer
(3) Work on the task until the time is up
(4) Take a 5 minute break
(5) Every 4 pomodoros take a longer 15-30 minute break

name: Accountability Partner
lead: Get an accountability partner to keep you on track
text: An accountability partner is someone with whom you establish an ongoing, reciprocal relationship.
You and your partner commit to coaching each other towards achieving your respective goals and holding each other accountable for your progress.
Accountability beats elaborate planning all the time.

name: Be a Lobster
lead: In order for the lobster to grow it must shed its hard, inelastic shell
text: Don't be a victim of your circumstances.
Be like the lobster - shed your shell and grow.
It might be hard. But if a lobster can do it, so can you.

name: Talk Is Cheap
lead: It's very easy to talk about values, goals and rules
text: But when people's actions contradict their talk, pay attention.
Anyone can say anything to anyone - it's all about action. Actions speak louder than words.

name: On Tape
lead: Talk as though you are being recorded
text: Keeping this in mind will help you be more aware of what you're saying.
It will sensitise you against gossip and reduces the chances of you feeling like "I wish I hadn't said that ..."

name: Tell Stories
lead: If you want to communicate anything, tell a story
text: Humans love stories. From our earliest childhood we have learned from, listened to and told stories.
Marketing is no longer about the stuff that you make, but about the stories you tell.

name: Be an Intern
lead: You never know what you'll learn or where you'll go by being willing to intern
text: Learn from others.
Regardless of what you have accomplished in one area of life, don't shy away from starting at the bottom in a different area.
If you want to be Mufasa, you must continue being Simba.

name: Sum of Parts
lead: The whole is greater than the sum of its parts
text: Often 2 + 2 = 5. The right combination of people, skills or ideas creates something none of them could alone. Look for pieces that complete each other.

name: Help Yourself
lead: Help yourself first, only then proceed to help others
text: On airplanes you are instructed to put on your own oxygen mask first, before you help others.
If you run out of oxygen, you will not be able to help anyone.

name: Eat Your Lunch
lead: Eat your lunch or somebody else will
text: Grab the opportunities that are in front of you.
If you don't, someone will.

name: Be Water
lead: Empty your mind, be formless
text: Shapeless, like water. If you put water into a cup, it becomes the cup. You put water into a bottle and it becomes the bottle. You put it in a teapot, it becomes the teapot. Now, water can flow or it can crash. Be water, my friend.
If there is a way, water will find it.
Be water my friend. Just flow.

name: Redefine the Problem
lead: When you redefine the problem you can come up with a superior solution
text: Mid 1990 Microsoft started an encyclopaedia called Encarta.
They employed all the right incentives. They paid professionals to write and edit thousands of articles.
Well compensated managers oversaw the project to ensure it came in on time and budget.
A few years later another encyclopaedia started. Their approach was radically different. Do it for fun. No one gets paid.
In 2009 Encarta was shut down. Today Wikipedia is the largest encyclopaedia in the world.

name: Peak State
lead: Before doing anything important, get into peak state
text: Peak state is a state of high mental alertness and high energy.
Move your body, jump around, smile and listen to motivating music.
Do anything to shake up your system. Remember, emotion follows motion.

name: First Seven Seconds
lead: Our brains make a thousand computations during the first seven seconds we see someone
text: Within seven seconds, the person across from you is assessing whether you are likeable, trustworthy, and competent.
Four tips for a great first impression: (1) Dress and groom appropriately (2) Smile (3) Speak slowly and clearly (4) Keep a good posture

name: Set Your Standard
lead: You get what you tolerate
text: Your standards set the bar for how others treat you and what you accept from yourself. Want to improve your life? Raise your standards.

name: Balance
lead: Life is like riding a bicycle
text: To keep your balance you must keep moving.

name: Burn the Boats
lead: Success comes from total commitments
text: If you want to take the island, burn the boats.

name: Find Your Tribe
lead: The most basic human need is belonging
text: Find and surround yourself with likeminded people.
To do this, be authentically you.

name: Interested Is Interesting
lead: Be interested in others to be interesting to them
text: You'll make more friends in two months by being interested in others than in two years trying to get others interested in you. Ask questions, and really listen.

name: Choose Your Pain
lead: You can choose between two pains: discipline or regret
text: While discipline weighs ounces, regret weighs tons.

The small "pain" of discipline brushing your teeth every day or tending to your relationships or staying true to what you believe in is a lot smaller than the pain of regret you will feel if you don't.

name: Ride the Wave
lead: Take advantage of momentum
text: Get on the board at the right time and let the wave carry you.

name: Take Cold Showers
lead: Start taking cold showers
text: Cold showers have a variety of benefits - Builds massive will power - Increases alertness - Reduce stress - Wakes you up / puts you to sleep - Improves skin and hair - Improves immunity and blood circulation - Stimulates weight loss
Start off by switching between warm and cold water at first and slowly increasing the duration of the cold water.
Try a five day challenge and see how it goes.

name: Domino Effect
lead: Take a little step that sets into motion increasingly larger results
text: Whatever you are trying to achieve or solve - find the "lead domino".
What is the action that makes everything else easier or obsolete?

name: Gratitude Is Power
lead: Gratitude changes your mood instantly
text: It's impossible to be mad and grateful at the same time. Choose gratitude. When you focus on what you have, you gain what you lack. When you focus on what you lack, you lose what you have.

name: Give Hugs
lead: Give (and receive) more hugs
text: Hugs reduce stress, improve communication, and lead to a happier and healthier life.
Oxytocin (the “cuddle hormone”) rises when we hug, touch, or sit close to someone else.
More oxytocin increases happiness and reduces stress.
Give hugs, be happy.

name: Low Hanging Fruits
lead: The lowest hanging fruits are the easiest to pick
text: When starting a project, complete the easiest tasks first.
Completing these will generate momentum which can be used to accomplish the larger tasks.

name: Top 20%
lead: Being in the top 1% in any category or domain is extremely difficult and rare
text: However, being in the top 20% in three different categories is quite easy.
Choose three categories where you can be in the top 20%. By combining three different domains you will be very unique.
For example, you might be a great engineer who also has an eye for design and is good at public speaking.

name: Dig Your Well
lead: Dig your well before you're thirsty
text: There is great wisdom in preparing for the inevitable.
The time to dig a well is not when you are weak and dying of thirst.
Plan ahead. Prepare.

name: Things Take Time
lead: You can't produce a baby in one month by getting nine women pregnant
text: No matter how great the talent or efforts, some things just take time.
Good things take time, be patient.
Most “overnight successes” take 5-10 years.
Remember, you are celebrated in public for the work you have done in private.

name: Play Pretend
lead: Fake it until you make it
text: You have to be before you can do (even if it's just in your mind) and you have to do before you can have.
Fool yourself into it and it will happen. Try it.

name: Leverage
lead: Get more out of what you already have
text: Leverage multiplies your effort. Look at your skills, time, money and network, and find ways to combine them so each one amplifies the others. Small inputs, big outputs.

name: Grow
lead: Intellectual growth should commence at birth and cease only at death
text: Make sure you do something that helps you grow every day.
Like everything, growth compounds.
Little by little a little becomes a lot.

name: Warrior
lead: Don't be a worrier
text: Be a warrior.
Worrying is like a rocking chair. It gives you something to do but it gets you nowhere

name: Eat Healthy Food
lead: Healthy food is good for your body, and your mind
text: You may notice that you feel tired and have trouble concentrating after a heavy meal.
Eat healthy food for optimal performance.

name: Face Your Fear
lead: What's on the other side of fear?
text: Nothing.
We are often more afraid of the thought than the reality of a specific event or instance.
Make a habit of facing your fears whenever you can.
This will help you get more comfortable and eventually overcome them.
The next time you say you can't, then you must.
This will get you in the habit of stretching your comfort zone.

name: Don't Fight Nature
lead: Look deep into nature and you will understand everything better
text: Nature will not change. Understand and accept or use it.
Whatever you do, don't fight it. You will lose.

name: Control Your Ego
lead: The true measure of a man is the degree to which he has managed to subjugate his ego
text: The more we learn, the more we realise how little we actually know.
The quieter you become, the more you are able to hear.

name: Visualize
lead: You have to see before you can do
text: For centuries it was believed that running a 4-minute mile was physically impossible. In 1954 Roger Bannister did it.
In addition to his physical practice, Roger practiced in his head. Over and over he envisioned himself breaking the 4 minute barrier.
Seeing is believing. By the end of 1957, 16 runners had broken the 4 minute mile.

name: Failure Feedback
lead: Embrace failure to achieve success
text: Risk failure again and again until you've learned all the lessons. There is no failure as long as you continue to learn and adapt. Reframe your thoughts around failure and replace the word with feedback. It's impossible to succeed without failure. All great success is preceded by great failure.

name: Toughen Up
lead: It's not how many times you get knocked down but how many times you get up
text: It's normal to feel sad, tired or uncomfortable sometimes. However, it's always only temporary.
When the going get tough, the tough get going.

name: Rig the Game
lead: Rig the game so you can win
text: Set yourself up to win. Compete where you have an unfair advantage. And if you don't have one, change your environment. Want to lose weight? Don't keep junk food in the house. Want to break a habit? Stay clear of the people who have it.

name: Be Honest
lead: No legacy is as rich as honesty
text: Honesty builds trust, and trust is the foundation of every good relationship. Tell the truth, even when it's uncomfortable. People will always know where they stand with you.

name: Own It
lead: Leaders must take ownership of anything in their world
text: If you want to lead, take responsibility.

name: Change Your Story
lead: Change your story, change your life
text: Eliminate limiting beliefs and invisible scripts. You are what you tell yourself.
Tell yourself you can or you can't - you'll be right either way.

name: Repot Yourself
lead: If you feel like you have stopped growing, repot yourself
text: If you put a plant into a bigger pot with new soil it will be able grow again.
Leave your comfort zone, try new things.

name: Improve 1%
lead: Improve one percent every day
text: Trying to improve something by 100% can be very daunting. Instead, improve 1% every day and day by day that will compound.
Leverage the power of compounding and little by little, a little becomes a lot.

name: Be Punctual
lead: Being punctual is an easy way to build a reputation of being reliable
text: It's an indicator of whether you mean what you say.
People always notice when you're late.
Respect their time, be punctual.

name: Think Win-Win
lead: In the long run, if it isn't a win, both parties lose
text: Win-win is the only option for long term success and happiness.
Whenever you interact with someone, make sure that both sides walk away feeling good.

name: Memento Mori
lead: Remember that you will die
text: Life is finite.
Treat it special and make the most out of it. Make time for things that bring you joy every day.

name: Be an Arrow
lead: What pulled you back can also be what propels you forward
text: A minor setback can prepare you for a major comeback.
It's not how many times you get knocked down that counts, it's how many times you get back up.

name: Complete Hilariously
lead: Whatever you're doing, have fun while doing it
text: Take any problem or task and add a metric that brings you joy.
For instance, dance while doing chores in the house or sing while you're working.

name: Persevere
lead: There is one Yes for every 99 No's
text: Don't be discouraged by people who tell you no.
Instead listen, learn and get excited. Each no gets you closer to the next yes.

name: Break It Down
lead: Break down large goals into small goals
text: We overestimate what we can achieve in one year and we underestimate what we can achieve in 10 years.
Humans are better at small things.
Take your 10 year goal and chop it into small, exciting one year goals. Take your one year goal and chop it into monthly or even weekly goals.
Writing a 400 page novel in one year would mean writing 7,5 pages per week or just over one page per day.

name: Remove Can't
lead: Remove "can't" from your vocabulary
text: Words create emotions, and emotions create actions. Once you remove "can't", you start looking for ways you can. That's very empowering.

name: Make Simple Rules
lead: If you want to get results, establish rules to achieve them
text: The easier the rule, the higher the likelihood of you following it.
Reduce to the ridiculous.

name: Morning Routine
lead: Your morning sets the tone of your entire day
text: If you win the first hour of the day, you win the day.
Experiment with different activities such as exercise, meditation, journaling or reading.
Make sure it is consistent and that you can stick to it.

name: Rock or Ballet
lead: You can either hold a successful ballet or rock concert - decide
text: Don't hold a ballet and advertise it as a rock concert.
You need to be clear on what you are offering.
If you do this effectively, people will self select automatically.

name: Be Present
lead: The only real reality is the present moment
text: The past is done and the future is yet to come.

name: Delay Gratification
lead: Delay immediate gratification for larger rewards later
text: When you do the things you need to do when you need to do them, the day will come when you can do the things you want to do when you want to do them.

name: Proximity Is Power
lead: Get close to people who already do what you want to do
text: Turn your dreams and goals into reality faster, by getting close to people who are already doing what you want to do. Be where they are to learn, and model what has already been proven to work.

name: Progress Not Perfection
lead: A person who has never made a mistake has never tried anything new
text: Fail early and fail often in order to succeed sooner.

name: Think Ahead
lead: Failing to plan is planning to fail
text: It's better to think ahead and plan, than to look back and regret.

name: Bug Book
lead: Study yourself like a bug and write your findings in a book
text: Observe your patterns, habits and behaviours to determine what you want to change.
Viewing yourself as a bug provides distance and removes judgement.
You can only improve what you measure.

name: Bamboo Theory
lead: The power of the Chinese bamboo plant
text: You water and fertilise for years with barely anything happening. Then, once the roots are in place, a new cane can grow up to 23 metres in just a few weeks.
The lesson: things take time, you reap what you sow and be consistent. If you stop watering in year 3 the bamboo won't grow in year 5.

name: Be a Bee
lead: Be a bee and cross pollinate
text: Take ideas or concepts from different places and combine them to make something new.
The best ideas come from mixing two or more seemingly unrelated things.

name: Meditate
lead: Meditation is fun, free, and for everyone
text: All you need is a few quiet minutes. It helps you de-stress, sleep better and see yourself more clearly. There's no right or wrong way. Just start.

name: Run Your Race
lead: When you're in a race, don't worry what the other runners are doing, just run
text: Don't compare your chapter one to someone else's chapter twenty.
Run your own race. Focus on being better than you were yesterday.

name: (Dis)comfort
lead: Get out of your comfort zone
text: Do things outside of your comfort zone. This is how you grow. Stretch it a little every day, and discomfort turns into comfort.

name: Good Stuff Sticks
lead: Things that are truly remarkable stay in peoples minds
text: If you want to make something people remember, make good stuff.

name: Say Thank You
lead: Saying thank you is the most simple form of gratitude
text: When you say thank you people feel appreciated and loved. Making others feel good brings good back to you in unexpected ways. It also makes you generally happier and healthier.

name: Think Big
lead: Your only limit is your mind
text: Think big. Start small.

name: Start With Why
lead: Start with why because reasons reap results
text: You need strong enough reasons to follow through, especially when things are not going well.

name: Shiny Objects
lead: SOS - Shiny Object Syndrome
text: Beware of getting distracted by new, exciting ideas or tools and leaving current projects unfinished. Opportunities that don't align with your goals are distractions. Stay narrow, stay deep. Stay clear of shiny objects.

name: Baby Steps
lead: A journey of a thousand miles starts with a single step
text: Take baby steps, but be consistent.
Most overnight successes are actually 10 years in the making.
You get rewarded in public for what you have practiced in private.

name: Monetize Your Growth
lead: Growth always requires training
text: Find out how you can get paid while training.
The Beatles trace their success to their time playing back-to-back shows in Hamburg, Germany.
The group got excessive practice and was paid £ 100 per week.
Much more than promoters in Liverpool paid.

name: Principles
lead: Principles are ways of successfully dealing with reality to get what you want out of life
text: Principles are fundamental truths that serve as the foundations for behaviour that gets you what you want out of life. They can be applied again and again in similar situations to help you achieve your goals.

name: Think Different
lead: What got you here won't get you there
text: To get a different result, you have to think differently. If you always use the same recipe, you'll always get the same cake. Want a better one? Change the ingredients, the quantities, the bake time. Think different.

name: Paint a Picture
lead: A picture is worth a thousand words
text: If you want to communicate effectively, paint a picture.
Paint with words, with paint or with whatever comes naturally.

name: Measure, Manage
lead: What gets measured gets managed
text: Set measurable goals.
Measure regularly and precisely.
This way you will know if you are moving closer to your goal or not.
If you consistently miss your goals, adjust your approach.
Learn, read, model or be an intern.

name: Opposites Attract
lead: Be open. Be kind. Be curious
text: You would be surprised how much you can have in common with someone completely different from you. Learn from one another and you will both grow.

name: Consistency Key
lead: Following a good plan regularly is better than following a perfect plan sometimes
text: Consistency compounds.
Whatever you want more of in your life, make sure that you are doing it consistently.
The more you do it, the more you get.

name: Puck Rule
lead: The only constant is change
text: Both in hockey and in life, there is constant change. Make sure you are aware and act accordingly. Skate to where the puck is going, not where it was.

name: Closer Targets
lead: Move your target closer
text: Practice easy goals.
Reaching an easy goal will give you confidence to replicate your success with harder goals.

name: Opportunity Bus
lead: Opportunities will come
text: Make sure you're ready to get on the bus when they do.

name: Remove Bottlenecks
lead: Get more done by finding and eliminating bottlenecks
text: Bottlenecks are limiting steps in a process.
If it takes you 20 minutes to drive to work and another 30 minutes to find parking, parking is your bottleneck.
Bottlenecks destroy productivity. Take a look at your typical day. Bottlenecks might be hiding in your schedule without you realising it.

name: Be Curious
lead: Cultivate curiosity
text: Don't judge, be curious.
If you want to grow, be as curious as a child. This way you will never stop learning.

name: Live Life
lead: Live life to the fullest and know what that means for you
text: You have to colour outside the lines once in a while if you want to make your life a masterpiece.
Laugh every day. Keep growing, keep dreaming, keep following your heart.
Right now is the wisest you've ever been and the youngest you'll ever be.
Take chances, live life.

name: Play
lead: How you behave while playing a game is also how you behave in other areas of life
text: Want to get to know someone better? Play a game with them.
Do they cheat? Do they have a temper? Are they super competitive?
How you do anything is how you do everything.

name: Be Kind
lead: Be kind
text: To yourself and to others.
You always have a choice. Choose kindness, it will rarely come back to bite you

name: Eat the Broccoli
lead: If you want results you must do the work
text: You can't live a healthy life without eating any "broccoli".
And the comforting truth is, you might even start liking it.
What's the thing you don't like but you know is good for you?
What's your broccoli?

name: Options Rule
lead: Have better options
text: It's not about how to best choose between options A and B.
Rather, make sure that A and B are both good options.
That way the final decision becomes less important.

name: Study Systems
lead: Success leaves clues
text: If someone consistently outperforms his peers in a certain task or area, then they aren't lucky. They've figured out a system.
Seek out the top performer in the field you want to improve in and save time by modelling them. Read their books, watch their videos and listen to their podcasts. Learn from their mistakes.
The harder you work the luckier you become.

name: Trigger Train
lead: Use triggers to build better habits
text: A trigger train is a selection of habits that you perform one after the other. For example, decide that every time you enter a room, you smile and stand tall. This will improve your confidence, your mood and all your interactions.

name: Write It Down
lead: Get things off your mind and onto paper
text: Writing things down frees up headspace and quiets the constant chatter known as monkey mind. Keep a notebook with you. Whenever something is on your mind, write it down.

name: Egg Basket Rule
lead: Don't put all your eggs in one basket
text: If you put all your effort into one thing and that thing does not work out, then you are left with nothing.
Diversify.

name: Just Ask
lead: Ask and you shall receive
text: Most people don't ask because they fear a no. If you don't ask, the answer is always no. So just ask. You'll be surprised how often the answer is yes.

name: Kaizen
lead: Kaizen is Japanese for continuous improvement
text: Every day, try to be a bit better than you were yesterday.
Make this a habit.
Things don't equal happiness, but progress does.

name: Make New Ways
lead: Where there's a will there's a way
text: Determination and willpower will overcome any obstacle.
If you want it you can do it. The question is just, how bad do you want it?

name: Screw Monday
lead: Whatever you're putting off, don't wait for “Monday“
text: Do it today. Do it now.
There's never a perfect time to start a project, diet, relationship or anything.
The best time is right now.

name: Own Your Niche
lead: Be a meaningful specific, not a wandering generality
text: Decide what is uniquely yours and grow from there. Find your niche. Only you can be you. Don't bother trying to be someone else.

name: Three Cs
lead: Three Cs to make things happen
text: (1) CHECK Research if there has been a similar situation or if this has been done before. If yes, use and adapt. You don't have to reinvent the wheel. (2) CONTACT Reach out to the people that you think could help you. Be relentless in your outreach. (3) CREATE Make a plan. Find like-minded people. Start.

name: Set Goals
lead: You can't achieve a goal you don't have
text: To achieve anything, you have to set goals. It gives you a direction and helps you focus on what is important. Start with small, easy goals and get into the habit of achieving them. This will give you momentum and confidence to tackle larger goals. Set SMART goals.

name: Be Clear
lead: Clarity is key
text: Always know what you want. And communicate it clearly. Use as few words as possible and as many as necessary. Remember the Rule of Threes: Never make more than three points. Explain difficult ideas in three different ways. Make important points three times.

name: Step by Step
lead: The secret of getting ahead is getting started
text: The secret of getting started is breaking your complex overwhelming tasks into small manageable tasks, and starting on the first one.

name: Who's It Serving
lead: Always ask yourself, who's it serving?
text: If something is not serving you and you don't have to do it, stop doing it. And when you're offered something, ask yourself, "Who is this really serving?" before you make a decision.

name: Smile
lead: Smiling instantly lifts your mood and lights up the room

name: Sharpen the Saw
lead: If you have six hours to cut down a tree, spend the first four hours sharpening the saw

name: Who Luck
lead: Seek out people who inspire, encourage and challenge you
text: “Who luck“ is the luck of finding the right mentor, partner, teammate, leader or friend. When luck turns bad, they will be here to help you. When times are good, they will celebrate with you.

name: Listen
lead: Listen with the intent to understand not with the intent to respond
text: Humans have two ears and one mouth. Use them in that proportion.

name: Feel Fabulous
lead: Figure out what makes you feel good and do it every day
text: Just make sure it's healthy and sustainable.

name: Love Yourself
lead: Be kind to yourself
text: The only person you are always with is you. Why go in anger, sadness or frustration? Love yourself.—— You can only love others to the extent you love yourself . Worry never robs tomorrow of its sorrow. It only saps today of its joy. Practice self love. (1) Stop criticising yourself. If you are always looking for what you are missing you will never be happy. (2) Don't take your thoughts that seriously, simply be a spectator. If others spoke to us the way we sometimes speak to ourselves we would not tolerate it.

name: Remove Ants
lead: Remove Automatic Negative Thoughts (ANTs) from your mind
text: ANTs are cynical, gloomy and complaining thoughts that seem to be coming all by themselves. These thoughts can become self-fulfilling prophecies. Remove them in three steps (1) Become aware of the thoughts (2) Challenge them (3) Replace them with positive, affirming thoughts

name: Five Ws
lead: Ask the five Ws
text: To get the complete picture, ask Who? What? Where? When? Why? Answer all five and you understand the situation. Skip one and you're guessing.

name: Choose Distractions
lead: Predetermine what you will do when you procrastinate
